cues.zh: 以下是与 Cursor 团队创始成员 Michael Truell、Sualeh Asif、Arvid Lunnemark 和 Aman Sanger 的对话。
cues.en: The following is a conversation with the founding members of the Cursor team, Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Arvid Lunnemark, and Aman Sanger.

cues.zh: Cursor 是一款基于 VS Code 的代码编辑器，为 AI 辅助编程增加了许多强大功能。
cues.en: Cursor is a code editor based on VS Code that adds a lot of powerful features for AI-assisted coding.

cues.zh: 它吸引了编程和 AI 社区的关注与热情。
cues.en: It has captivated the attention and excitement of the programming and AI communities.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个绝佳机会，深入探讨 AI 在编程中的角色。
cues.en: So I thought this is an excellent opportunity to dive deep into the role of AI in programming.

cues.zh: 这是一场技术性极强的对话，意义远超一款代码编辑器。
cues.en: This is a super technical conversation that is bigger than just about one code editor.

cues.zh: 它关乎编程的未来，也关乎人类与 AI 协作设计和工程化复杂而强大系统的未来。
cues.en: It’s about the future of programming and in general, the future of human AI collaboration in designing and engineering complicated and powerful systems.

cues.zh: 这是 Lex Fridman 播客。
cues.en: This is the Lex Fridman podcast.

cues.zh: 想支持我们，请查看简介中的赞助商。
cues.en: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

cues.zh: 现在，亲爱的朋友们，有请 Michael、Sualeh、Arvid 和 Aman。
cues.en: And now, dear friends, here’s Michael, Sualeh, Arvid and Aman.

cues.zh: 好的，这太棒了。
cues.en: All right, this is awesome.

cues.zh: 我们有来自 Cursor 团队的 Michael、Aman、Sualeh、Arvid。
cues.en: We have Michael, Aman, Sualeh, Arvid here from the Cursor team.

cues.zh: 首先，一个大而无厘头的问题。
cues.en: First up, big ridiculous question.

cues.zh: 代码编辑器的意义是什么？
cues.en: What’s the point of a code editor?

cues.zh: 所以代码编辑器基本上就是你构建软件的地方，而今天或者说很长一段时间以来，这意味着你文本编辑正式编程语言的地方。
cues.en: So the code editor is largely the place where you build software and today or for a long time, that’s meant the place where you text edit a formal programming language.

cues.zh: 对于不是程序员的人来说，可以把代码编辑器想成给程序员用的超级增强版文字处理器，之所以说是增强版，是因为代码有大量结构。
cues.en: And for people who aren’t programmers, the way to think of a code editor is a really souped up word processor for programmers, where the reason it’s souped up is code has a lot of structure.

cues.zh: 因此，这个“文字处理器”——代码编辑器，实际上能为你做很多文字处理器在写作领域一直无法为编辑文本的人做到的事情。
cues.en: And so the “word processor,” the code editor can actually do a lot for you that word processors sort of in the writing space haven’t been able to do for people editing texts there.

cues.zh: 从为代码中的实际 token 提供视觉区分，让你能快速扫读，到让你在代码库中导航，就像用超链接在互联网上浏览一样，跳转到你所使用内容的定义，再到错误检查以捕捉基础 bug，这些都已经涵盖了。
cues.en: And so that’s everything from giving you visual differentiation of the actual tokens in the code so you can scan it quickly to letting you navigate around the code base, sort of like you’re navigating around the internet with hyperlinks, you’re going to definitions of things you’re using to error checking to catch rudimentary bugs.

cues.zh: 传统上，这就是代码编辑器的含义。
cues.en: And so traditionally that’s what a code editor has meant.

cues.zh: 而我认为，代码编辑器的定义在未来 10 年会发生很大变化，因为构建软件的含义可能开始变得有些不同。
cues.en: And I think that what a code editor is is going to change a lot over the next 10 years as what it means to build software maybe starts to look a bit different.

cues.zh: 我还觉得代码编辑器就应该好玩。
cues.en: I think also a code editor should just be fun.

cues.zh: 是的，这非常重要。
cues.en: Yes, that is very important.

cues.zh: 这非常重要。
cues.en: That is very important.

cues.zh: 而这实际上在我们决定构建什么时，是一个有点被低估的方面。
cues.en: And it’s actually sort of an underrated aspect of how we decide what to build.

cues.zh: 我们构建很多东西，然后去尝试，做个实验，结果又把它扔掉，因为不好玩。
cues.en: A lot of the things that we build and then we try them out, we do an experiment and then we actually throw them out because they’re not fun.

cues.zh: 而好玩很大程度上往往就是快。
cues.en: And so a big part of being fun is being fast a lot of the time.

cues.zh: 快就是好玩。
cues.en: Fast is fun.

cues.zh: 对，快就是……这该印在T恤上。
cues.en: Yeah, fast is… That should be a T-shirt.

cues.zh: 从根本上说，我觉得吸引很多人用电脑做东西的原因之一，就是这种疯狂的迭代速度。在其他领域，你可能会受限于资源或能力……甚至能把一大群人聚在一起写代码这件事本身就很神奇，就你和电脑，单凭这一点，你就能很快做出很酷的东西。
cues.en: Fundamentally, I think one of the things that draws a lot of people to building stuff on computers is this insane iteration speed, where in other disciplines you might be sort of gate capped by resources or the ability… Even the ability to get a large group together and coding is this amazing thing where it’s you and the computer and that alone, you can build really cool stuff really quickly.

cues.zh: 给不了解的人介绍一下，Cursor 是一款超酷的新编辑器，是 VS Code 的一个分支。
cues.en: So for people who don’t know, Cursor is this super cool new editor that’s a fork of VS Code.

cues.zh: 很想听听你讲讲自己用过的编辑器历程。
cues.en: It would be interesting to get your explanation of your own journey of editors.

cues.zh: 我想你们大家都是 VS Code 加 Copilot 的忠实用户。
cues.en: I think all of you were big fans of VS Code with Copilot.

cues.zh: 你是怎么开始用 VS Code 的，又是怎么一路走到 Cursor 的？
cues.en: How did you arrive to VS Code and how did that lead to your journey with Cursor?

cues.zh: 是啊，我觉得我们很多人……其实我们所有人最初都是 [听不清 00:03:39] 的用户。
cues.en: Yeah, so I think a lot of us… Well, all of us were originally [inaudible 00:03:39] users.

cues.zh: 纯 Vim。
cues.en: Pure Vim.

cues.zh: 纯 Vim。
cues.en: Pure Vim.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 不是 Neovim，就是纯 Vim 加终端。
cues.en: No Neovim, just Pure Vim and a terminal.

cues.zh: 至少对我来说，大概是在 Copilot 出来那会儿，也就是 2021 年，我特别想试试。
cues.en: And at least for myself, it was around the time that Copilot came out, so 2021 that I really wanted to try it.

cues.zh: 于是我用了 VS Code，那是当时唯一能用它的代码编辑器，虽然我很喜欢用 Vim，但 Copilot 在 VS Code 里的体验足够好，说服我换了过去。
cues.en: So I went into VS Code, the only code editor in which it was available, and even though I really enjoyed using Vim, just the experience of Copilot with VS Code was more than good enough to convince me to switch.

cues.zh: 所以那基本就成了默认选择，直到我们开始做 Cursor。
cues.en: And so that kind of was the default until we started working on Cursor.

cues.zh: 也许我们应该解释一下 Copilot 是做什么的。
cues.en: And maybe we should explain what Copilot does.

cues.zh: 它是一个非常好用的自动补全工具。
cues.en: It’s a really nice auto complete.

cues.zh: 当你开始写代码时，它会建议一两行或三行来补全代码。
cues.en: As you start writing a thing, it suggests one or two or three lines how to complete the thing.

cues.zh: 这其中有一种有趣的体验。
cues.en: And there’s a fun experience in that.

cues.zh: 就像当你和好朋友关系亲密时，朋友能接上你要说的话？
cues.en: You know like when you have a close friendship and your friend completes your sentences?

cues.zh: 当它做得好时，会有一种亲密的感觉。
cues.en: When it’s done well, there’s an intimate feeling.

cues.zh: 也许有比“亲密”更好的词，但那种“哇，它懂我”的感觉很酷。
cues.en: There’s probably a better word than intimate, but there’s a cool feeling of holy shit, it gets me.

cues.zh: 而当它不懂你时，就会有不愉快的感觉。
cues.en: And then there’s an unpleasant feeling when it doesn’t get you.

cues.zh: 所以就有那种摩擦感。
cues.en: And so there’s that kind of friction.

cues.zh: 但我想说，对很多人来说，“它懂我”的感觉压过了“它不懂我”的失落。
cues.en: But I would say for a lot of people, the feeling that it gets me overpowers that it doesn’t.

cues.zh: 而且我觉得 Github Copilot 一个被低估的方面是，即使它错了，虽然有点烦人，但也没那么糟，因为你只需要再输入一个字符，也许它就能懂你了，或者再输入一个字符，它就能懂你了。
cues.en: And I think actually one of the underrated aspects of Github Copilot is that even when it’s wrong, it’s a little bit annoying, but it’s not that bad because you just type another character and then maybe then it gets you, or you type another character and then it gets you.

cues.zh: 所以即使它错了，也没那么糟。
cues.en: So even when it’s wrong, it’s not that bad.

cues.zh: 你可以反复迭代、修正它。
cues.en: You can sort of iterate and fix it.

cues.zh: 对我来说，Copilot 另一个被低估的地方在于，它是第一个真正的 AI 产品。
cues.en: I mean, the other underrated part of Copilot for me was just the first real AI product.

cues.zh: 也就是第一个语言模型消费级产品。
cues.en: So the first language model consumer product.

cues.zh: 所以 Copilot 算是语言模型的第一个杀手级应用。
cues.en: So Copilot was kind of like the first killer app for LMs.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 测试版在 2021 年就发布了。
cues.en: And the beta was out in 2021.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那 Cursor 的起源故事是什么？
cues.en: So what’s the origin story of Cursor?

cues.zh: 大概在 2020 年，OpenAI 发表了 scaling loss 论文，那一刻，这个领域看起来有了清晰可预测的进展——即使我们没有更多新想法，只要有更多算力和数据，就能让这些模型好很多。
cues.en: So around 2020, the scaling loss papers came out from OpenAI and that was a moment where this looked like clear predictable progress for the field where even if we didn’t have any more ideas, it looked like you could make these models a lot better if you had more compute and more data.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，关于 scaling loss 这个话题，我们大概能聊三四个小时。
cues.en: By the way, we’ll probably talk for three to four hours on the topic of scaling loss.

cues.zh: 简单总结一下，这是一系列论文和想法中的一篇，说的是在机器学习领域，模型规模和数据规模可能越大越好。
cues.en: But just to summarize, it’s a paper in a set of papers in a set of ideas that say bigger might be better for model size and data size in the realm of machine learning.

cues.zh: 更大更好，但是可预测地更好。
cues.en: It’s bigger and better, but predictably better.

cues.zh: 好了，那是另一个话题了。
cues.en: Okay, that’s another topic of conversation.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以大概在那段时间，我们中有些人有很多概念性的讨论：这会变成什么样？
cues.en: So around that time for some of us, there were a lot of conceptual conversations about what’s this going to look like?

cues.zh: 对于所有这些不同的知识工作者领域，故事会怎么讲——这项技术变好会如何让他们变得更好？
cues.en: What’s the story going to be for all these different knowledge worker fields about how they’re going to be made better by this technology getting better?

cues.zh: 然后我觉得有几个时刻，论文中预测的理论收益开始变得非常具体，开始感觉像是一个时刻——如果你想在AI领域做有用的工作，你其实可以不用读博士了。
cues.en: And then I think there were a couple of moments where the theoretical gains predicted in that paper started to feel really concrete and it started to feel like a moment where you could actually go and not do a PhD if you wanted to do useful work in AI.

cues.zh: 现在感觉真的能搭建出一整套非常有用的系统了。
cues.en: It actually felt like now there was this whole set of systems one could build that were really useful.

cues.zh: 我想第一个时刻我们已经聊过一点了，就是玩 Copilot 早期 beta 版的时候，那感觉既棒又神奇。
cues.en: And I think that the first moment we already talked about a little bit, which was playing with the early beta of Copilot, that was awesome and magical.

cues.zh: 我觉得下一个重大时刻，一切开始串联起来，其实是拿到了 GPT-IV 的早期访问权限。
cues.en: I think that the next big moment where everything kind of clicked together was actually getting early access to GPT-IV.

cues.zh: 大概是 2022 年底，我们开始捣鼓那个模型，能力的跃升感觉非常巨大。
cues.en: So it was sort of end of 2022 was when we were tinkering with that model and the step-upping capabilities felt enormous.

cues.zh: 在那之前，我们一直在做几个不同的项目。
cues.en: And previous to that, we had been working on a couple of different projects.

cues.zh: 因为 Copilot，因为规模化的可能性，也因为我们之前对这项技术的兴趣，我们一直在捣鼓面向程序员的工具，但都是非常具体的东西。
cues.en: Because of Copilot, because of scaling odds, because of our prior interest in the technology, we had been tinkering around with tools for programmers, but things that are very specific.

cues.zh: 我们当时在为金融专业人士构建工具，他们必须在 Jupyter Notebook 里工作，或者琢磨能不能用这些模型做静态分析？
cues.en: So we were building tools for financial professionals who have to work within a Jupyter Notebook or playing around with can you do static analysis with these models?

cues.zh: 然后 GPT- IV 的跃升让人觉得，看，这真的让我们之前预测的理论收益变得具体了。
cues.en: And then the step-up in GPT- IV felt like, look, that really made concrete the theoretical gains that we had predicted before.

cues.zh: 感觉在那个时间点，你立刻就能构建更多东西。
cues.en: It felt like you could build a lot more just immediately at that point in time.

cues.zh: 而且如果我们保持一致的话，真的感觉这不会只是一个点状解决方案。
cues.en: And also if we were being consistent, it really felt like this wasn’t just going to be a point solution thing.

cues.zh: 这将是整个编程都将通过这些模型来流转，感觉这需要一种不同类型的编程环境，一种不同类型的编程。
cues.en: This was going to be all of programming was going to flow through these models and it felt like that demanded a different type of programming environment, a different type of programming.

cues.zh: 所以大约在那时，我们就开始着手构建那种更大的愿景。
cues.en: And so we set off to build that sort of larger vision around then.

cues.zh: 有一件事我记得特别清楚。
cues.en: There’s one that I distinctly remember.

cues.zh: 我的室友是 IMO 金牌得主，美国有个叫 PUTNAM 的竞赛，算是大学生版的 IMO，是一场数学竞赛。
cues.en: So my roommate is an IMO Gold winner and there’s a competition in the US called the PUTNAM, which is sort of the IMO for college people and it’s this math competition.

cues.zh: 它特别厉害。
cues.en: It’s exceptionally good.

cues.zh: 我记得 2022 年 6 月前后，Shengtong 和 Aman 打了个赌，赌 2024 年 6 月或 7 月能不能用模型拿下 IMO 金牌。
cues.en: So Shengtong and Aman I remember, sort of June of 2022, had this bet on whether the 2024 June or July you were going to win a gold medal in the IMO with models.

cues.zh: IMO 就是国际数学奥林匹克。
cues.en: IMO is the International Math Olympiad.

cues.zh: 对，IMO 就是国际数学奥林匹克。
cues.en: Yeah, IMO is International Math Olympiad.

cues.zh: Arvid 和我当时也都在参赛。
cues.en: And so Arvid and I are both also competing in it.

cues.zh: 所以这事有点私人，我记得当时想，Matt，这不可能发生。
cues.en: So it was sort of personal and I remember thinking, Matt, this is not going to happen.

cues.zh: 虽然我算是相信进步，但我觉得 IMO 金牌这事，Aman 是在妄想。
cues.en: Even though I sort of believed in progress, I thought IMO Gold, Aman is delusional.

cues.zh: 说实话，我很清楚，我错得离谱。
cues.en: And to be honest, I mean, I was, to be clear, very wrong.

cues.zh: 但这可能是全组最有先见之明的赌注。
cues.en: But that was maybe the most prescient bet in the group.

cues.zh: 所以 DeepMind 的新结果证明，你是对的。
cues.en: So the new results from DeepMind, it turned out that you were correct.

cues.zh: 严格来说不算对。
cues.en: Technically not.

cues.zh: 严格来说不对，但只差一点。
cues.en: Technically incorrect but one point away.

cues.zh: Aman 当时对这东西特别热情，在那之前，Aman 有件 scaling loss 的T恤，他总穿着到处走，上面印着图表和公式。
cues.en: Aman was very enthusiastic about this stuff back then and before, Aman had this scaling loss T-shirt that he would wear around where it had the charts and the formulas on it.

cues.zh: 所以你是感受到了 AGI，还是感受到了 scaling loss？
cues.en: So you felt the AGI or you felt the scaling loss.

cues.zh: 对，我清楚地记得，在我还没深入批判性地思考 scaling laws 之前，和 Michael 有过一次对话，他提出了一个问题：为什么 scaling 不是你所需要的一切？或者为什么 scaling 不会带来巨大的进展？
cues.en: Yeah, I distinctly remember there was this one conversation I had with Michael before I hadn’t thought super deeply and critically about scaling laws and he kind of posed the question, why isn’t scaling all you need or why isn’t scaling going to result in massive gains in progress?

cues.zh: 我想我经历了悲伤的几个阶段。
cues.en: And I think I went through the stages of grief.

cues.zh: 先是愤怒、否认，最后想到这件事时，也就接受了。
cues.en: There is anger, denial, and then finally at the end just thinking about it, acceptance.

cues.zh: 从那以后，我对进展一直抱有希望，也比较乐观。
cues.en: And I think I’ve been quite hopeful and optimistic about progress since.

cues.zh: 我想先说明一点，这也要看你在哪些领域能看到进展。
cues.en: I think one thing I’ll caveat is I think it also depends on which domains you’re going to see progress.

cues.zh: 数学是个很好的领域，尤其是形式化定理证明，因为你能得到绝佳的验证信号，确认它到底对不对。
cues.en: Math is a great domain especially formal theorem proving because you get this fantastic signal of actually verifying if the thing was correct.

cues.zh: 所以这意味着像 RL 这样的方法能运转得非常好，而且我觉得你完全可以有在数学上远超人类的系统，但严格来说它仍然不算 AGI。
cues.en: And so this means something like RL can work really, really well and I think you could have systems that are perhaps very superhuman in math and still not technically have AGI.

cues.zh: 好，那我们能不能一路讲到 Cursor。
cues.en: Okay, so can we take it all the way to Cursor.

cues.zh: Cursor 是什么？
cues.en: And what is Cursor?

cues.zh: 它是 VS Code 的一个分支，而 VS Code 长期以来都是最流行的编辑器之一。
cues.en: It’s a fork of VS Code and VS Code is one of the most popular editors for a long time.

cues.zh: 大家都爱上了它。
cues.en: Everybody fell in love with it.

cues.zh: 大家都离开了 Vim，我为了它离开了 DMAX。
cues.en: Everybody left Vim, I left DMAX for it.

cues.zh: 抱歉。
cues.en: Sorry.

cues.zh: 它以一种根本性的方式，把开发者社区统一了起来。
cues.en: So unified in some fundamental way the developer community.

cues.zh: 然后你审视整个领域，观察 scaling laws，AI 正变得惊人地强大，于是你决定，仅靠 VS Code 写个扩展已经不够了，因为那有太多限制。
cues.en: And then you look at the space of things, you look at the scaling laws, AI is becoming amazing and you decided okay, it’s not enough to just write an extension via VS Code because there’s a lot of limitations to that.

cues.zh: 如果 AI 会持续变得越来越好，我们就必须真正重新思考，AI 该如何融入编辑过程。
cues.en: If AI is going to keep getting better and better and better, we need to really rethink how the AI is going to be part of the editing process.

cues.zh: 于是你决定 fork VS Code，开始打造许多我们接下来会聊到的出色功能。
cues.en: And so you decided to fork VS Code and start to build a lot of the amazing features we’ll be able to talk about.

cues.zh: 但做出这个决定是什么感觉？
cues.en: But what was that decision like?

cues.zh: 因为 VS Code 上有很多扩展，包括 Copilot，都在做类似 AI 的事情。
cues.en: Because there’s a lot of extensions, including Copilot, of VS Code that are doing sort of AI type stuff.

cues.zh: 当时决定直接 fork VS Code 是怎么考虑的？
cues.en: What was the decision like to just fork VS Code?

cues.zh: 所以做编辑器的决定对我们来说几乎是显而易见的，至少从我们想做的事和想达成的目标来看是这样，因为当我们开始做这个编辑器时，想法是这些模型会变得更强，能力会不断提升，并且会彻底改变你构建软件的方式，一方面是生产力会大幅提升，另一方面是更根本的，构建软件的方式会发生很大变化。
cues.en: So the decision to do an editor seemed kind of self-evident to us for at least what we wanted to do and achieve because when we started working on the editor, the idea was these models are going to get much better, their capabilities are going to improve and it’s going to entirely change how you build software, both in a you will have big productivity gains but also radical and now the active building software is going to change a lot.

cues.zh: 所以如果你是现有编码环境的一个插件，你对代码编辑器的控制就非常有限，而我们不想被这些限制锁死。
cues.en: And so you’re very limited in the control you have over a code editor if you’re a plugin to an existing coding environment and we didn’t want to get locked in by those limitations.

cues.zh: 我们希望能直接构建最有用的东西。
cues.en: We wanted to be able to just build the most useful stuff.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那么自然的问题是，VS Code 和 Copilot 算是竞争对手，你们怎么赢？
cues.en: Well then the natural question is, VS Code is kind of with Copilot a competitor, so how do you win?

cues.zh: 基本上就是靠速度和功能质量吗？
cues.en: Is it basically just the speed and the quality of the features?

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得这个领域很有意思，也许相当独特，因为回顾以往的技术浪潮，可能只有一件大事发生，然后开启一波新公司，但如今每一年、每一次模型能力的提升或跃迁，都会解锁一波新功能、新的可能性，尤其是在编程领域。
cues.en: Yeah, I mean I think this is a space that is quite interesting, perhaps quite unique where if you look at previous tech waves, maybe there’s kind of one major thing that happened and it unlocked a new wave of companies, but every single year, every single model capability or jump you get in model capabilities, you now unlock this new wave of features, things that are possible, especially in programming.

cues.zh: 所以我认为在 AI 编程领域，哪怕只领先几个月，更别说领先一年，都会让你的产品有用得多得多。
cues.en: And so I think in AI programming, being even just a few months ahead, let alone a year ahead makes your product much, much, much more useful.

cues.zh: 我觉得一年之后的 Cursor，会让今天的 Cursor 显得过时。
cues.en: I think the Cursor a year from now will need to make the Cursor of today look obsolete.

cues.zh: 我认为微软做了很多很棒的事情，但我不觉得他们处于一个能真正持续创新、像创业公司那样推动这件事的好位置。
cues.en: And I think Microsoft has done a number of fantastic things, but I don’t think they’re in a great place to really keep innovating and pushing on this in the way that a startup can.

cues.zh: 就是快速实现功能。
cues.en: Just rapidly implementing features.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 并且做那种真正能突破上限所需的研究和实验。
cues.en: And kind of doing the research experimentation necessary to really push the ceiling.

cues.zh: 我不太会从功能的角度去想，而是从为程序员提供的能力的角度去想。
cues.en: I don’t know if I think of it in terms of features as I think of it in terms of capabilities for programmers.

cues.zh: 随着新的 O1 模型出来，我相信还会有更多不同类型的模型，比如更长上下文、也许更快的，有各种疯狂的想法可以尝试，希望其中 10% 的疯狂想法能变成某种又酷又有用的东西，我们希望人们能更早用上它。
cues.en: As the new O1 model came out, and I’m sure there are going to be more models of different types, like longer context and maybe faster, there’s all these crazy ideas that you can try and hopefully 10% of the crazy ideas will make it into something kind of cool and useful and we want people to have that sooner.

cues.zh: 换个说法，一个被低估的事实是：我们是在为自己做这件事。
cues.en: To rephrase, an underrated fact is we’re making it for ourself.

cues.zh: 我们创办 Cursor 的时候，确实感受到了那种沮丧——模型……你能看到模型在变好，但 Copilot 的体验一直没变。
cues.en: When we started Cursor, you really felt this frustration that models… You could see models getting better, but the Copilot experience had not changed.

cues.zh: 就像，天啊，这些家伙，天花板越来越高，他们为什么不做新东西？
cues.en: It was like, man, these guys, the ceiling is getting higher, why are they not making new things?

cues.zh: 他们应该做新东西。
cues.en: They should be making new things.

cues.zh: 那些 alpha 功能都去哪儿了？
cues.en: Where’s all the alpha features?

cues.zh: 根本没有什么 alpha 功能。
cues.en: There were no alpha features.

cues.zh: 我确信它卖得很好。
cues.en: I’m sure it was selling well.

cues.zh: 我确信它是个很棒的生意，但感觉……我是那种特别想尝试和使用新东西的人，而很长一段时间里都没有新东西。
cues.en: I’m sure it was a great business, but it didn’t feel… I’m one of these people that really want to try and use new things and there was no new thing for a very long while.

cues.zh: 是啊，挺有意思的。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s interesting.

cues.zh: 我不知道你怎么用语言形容，但当你把 Cursor 和 Copilot 对比时，不知为何 Copilot 很快就让人觉得过时了。
cues.en: I don’t know how you put that into words, but when you compare a Cursor with Copilot, Copilot pretty quickly started to feel stale for some reason.

cues.zh: 对，我觉得有一点对我们很有帮助：我们是在同一个团队里同时做这些事，一边开发用户体验和与模型交互的方式，一边开发怎么让模型给出更好的答案。
cues.en: Yeah, I think one thing that I think helps us is that we’re sort of doing it all in one where we’re developing the UX and the way you interact with the model at the same time as we’re developing how we actually make the model give better answers.

cues.zh: 比如怎么构建提示词，怎么找到上下文，还有 Cursor Tab 的模型怎么训练？
cues.en: So how you build up the prompt or how do you find the context and for a Cursor Tab, how do you train the model?

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这有帮助，因为整件事都是同一批人在做，覆盖整个体验。
cues.en: So I think that helps us to have all of it the same people working on the entire experience [inaudible 00:15:17] .

cues.zh: 对，就像做 UI 的人和训练模型的人坐得大概只有 18 英尺远——
cues.en: Yeah, it’s like the person making the UI and the person training the model sit like 18 feet away-

cues.zh: 常常甚至是同一个人。
cues.en: Often the same person even.

cues.zh: 对，常常就是同一个人。
cues.en: Yeah, often even the same person.

cues.zh: 你能做出一些如果彼此不沟通、不做实验就根本不可能实现的东西。
cues.en: You can create things that are sort of not possible if you’re not talking, you’re not experimenting.

cues.zh: 你刚说你在用 Cursor 写 Cursor？
cues.en: And you’re using, like you said, Cursor to write Cursor?

cues.zh: 当然。
cues.en: Of course.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Oh yeah.

cues.zh: 那我们来聊聊其中一些功能吧。
cues.en: Well let’s talk about some of these features.

cues.zh: 聊聊那个无所不知、无所不能、赞美 Tab 吧，基本上就是加强版的自动补全。
cues.en: Let’s talk about the all-knowing the all-powerful praise be to the Tab, auto complete on steroids basically.

cues.zh: 那 Tab 是怎么工作的？
cues.en: So how does Tab work?

cues.zh: Tab 是什么？
cues.en: What is Tab?

cues.zh: 从高层面概括一下，我会说 Cursor 目前有两件事做得相当不错。
cues.en: To highlight and summarize at a high level, I’d say that there are two things that Cursor is pretty good at right now.

cues.zh: 它还能做别的事，但有两件事能帮到程序员。
cues.en: There are other things that it does, but two things that it helps programmers with.

cues.zh: 一个是这种在你肩后盯着、像个超快的同事，能跳到你前面打字，猜出你下一步要做什么。
cues.en: One is this idea of looking over your shoulder and being a really fast colleague who can kind of jump ahead of you and type and figure out what you’re going to do next.

cues.zh: 这就是最初的想法……一个好自动补全的核心思路就是预测你下一步要做什么，但你可以把这个概念做得更有野心，不只是预测光标后面的字符，而是真正预测你接下来要做的整个改动、下一个 diff、下一个要跳转的位置。
cues.en: And that was the original idea behind… That was kind of the kernel of the idea behind a good auto complete was predicting what you’re going to do next, but you can make that concept even more ambitious by not just predicting the characters after your Cursor but actually predicting the next entire change you’re going to make, the next diff, next place you’re going to jump to.

cues.zh: Cursor 现在很擅长的第二件事，是有时能帮你跑到 AI 前面，告诉它该做什么，从指令直接到代码。
cues.en: And the second thing Cursor is pretty good at right now too is helping you sometimes jump ahead of the AI and tell it what to do and go from instructions to code.

cues.zh: 这两方面我们都做了大量工作，让编辑体验更顺手，也让这些功能更智能、更快速。
cues.en: And on both of those we’ve done a lot of work on making the editing experience for those things ergonomic and also making those things smart and fast.

cues.zh: 我们特别想要的一件事，就是让模型能替我们编辑代码。
cues.en: One of the things we really wanted was we wanted the model to be able to edit code for us.

cues.zh: 这算是个愿望，在拿到能帮你编辑代码的好模型之前，我们尝试过很多次。
cues.en: That was kind of a wish and we had multiple attempts at it before we had a good model that could edit code for you.

cues.zh: 有了好模型之后，我觉得大家花了很多精力让推理变快，以获得好的体验，我们也开始融入……我是说，Michael 提到过跳到不同位置的能力，而这种跳转我觉得源于一种感觉：一旦你接受了一处编辑，就会想，天哪，下一步该去哪儿应该是一目了然的。
cues.en: Then after we had a good model, I think there’ve been a lot of effort to make the inference fast for having a good experience, and we’ve been starting to incorporate… I mean, Michael sort of mentioned this ability to jump to different places and that jump to different places I think came from a feeling of once you accept an edit, it’s like man, it should be just really obvious where to go next.

cues.zh: 就像我做了这个改动，模型应该直接知道下一个要去的地方在下面18行。
cues.en: It’s like I’d made this change, the model should just know that the next place to go to is 18 lines down.

cues.zh: 如果你是WIM用户，你可以按18JJ之类的，但我为什么要这么做呢？
cues.en: If you’re a WIM user, you could press 18JJ or whatever, but why am I doing this?

cues.zh: 模型应该直接知道。
cues.en: The model should just know it.

cues.zh: 所以想法是，你只需按Tab，它就会往下跳18行，然后展示下一个编辑，你再按Tab，只要你能一直按Tab就行。
cues.en: So the idea was you just press Tab, it would go 18 lines down and then show you the next edit and you would press Tab, so as long as you could keep pressing Tab.

cues.zh: 所以内部竞争就是，我们能让人按多少次Tab？
cues.en: And so the internal competition was, how many Tabs can we make someone press?

cues.zh: 一旦你有了这个想法，更抽象地说，要思考的是这些编辑怎么做到零熵？
cues.en: Once you have the idea, more abstractly, the thing to think about is how are the edits zero entropy?

cues.zh: 所以一旦你表达了意图，编辑就是……完成你的想法没有新的信息比特，但你仍然要输入一些字符让计算机理解你实际在想什么，那么也许模型就应该直接读懂你的心思，所有零熵的部分就应该被Tab掉。
cues.en: So once you’ve expressed your intent and the edit is… There’s no new bits of information to finish your thought, but you still have to type some characters to make the computer understand what you’re actually thinking, then maybe the model should just sort of read your mind and all the zero entropy bits should just be like tabbed away.

cues.zh: 那算是抽象版本。
cues.en: That was sort of the abstract version.

cues.zh: 有个有趣的现象：如果你看语言模型在不同领域的损失，我记得代码的每字节比特数（一种字符归一化的损失）比自然语言更低，这意味着代码里有很多 token 是超级可预测的，很多字符也是超级可预测的。
cues.en: There’s this interesting thing where if you look at language model loss on different domains, I believe the bits per byte, which is a kind of character normalize loss for code is lower than language, which means in general there are a lot of tokens in code that are super predictable, a lot of characters that are super predictable.

cues.zh: 而且我认为，当你不只是尝试自动补全代码，而是在预测用户在编辑现有代码时下一步会做什么，这一点会更加明显。
cues.en: And this is I think even magnified when you’re not just trying to auto complete code, but predicting what the user’s going to do next in their editing of existing code.

cues.zh: 所以 Cursor Tab 的目标就是：消除你在编辑器里所有低熵的操作。
cues.en: And so the goal of Cursor Tab is let’s eliminate all the low entropy actions you take inside of the editor.

cues.zh: 当意图实际上已经确定时，我们就直接把你快进到未来，跳过中间步骤。
cues.en: When the intent is effectively determined, let’s just jump you forward in time, skip you forward.

cues.zh: 那么，下一处 Cursor 预测的直觉和技术细节是怎样的？
cues.en: Well, what’s the intuition and what’s the technical details of how to do next Cursor prediction?

cues.zh: 那个跳转，我觉得对很多人来说并不那么直观。
cues.en: That jump, that’s not so intuitive I think to people.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我想我可以谈谈如何让这些东西运作起来的一些细节。
cues.en: I think I can speak to a few of the details on how to make these things work.

cues.zh: 它们的延迟极低，所以需要针对这个任务训练小模型。
cues.en: They’re incredibly low latency, so you need to train small models on this task.

cues.zh: 特别是，它们极度依赖 pre-fill token。
cues.en: In particular, they’re incredibly pre-fill token hungry.

cues.zh: 这意味着它们有非常非常长的提示，能看到你大量的代码，但实际上并不会生成那么多 token。
cues.en: What that means is they have these really, really long prompts where they see a lot of your code and they’re not actually generating that many tokens.

cues.zh: 所以最适合的方案是使用稀疏模型，也就是 MOE 模型。
cues.en: And so the perfect fit for that is using a sparse model, meaning an MOE model.

cues.zh: 这是我们取得的一个突破，大幅提升了它在长上下文下的性能。
cues.en: So that was one breakthrough we made that substantially improved its performance at longer context.

cues.zh: 另一个是我们构建的一种推测解码变体，叫做推测编辑。
cues.en: The other being a variant of speculative decoding that we built out called speculative edits.

cues.zh: 我认为，这两点是让它质量高又速度快的重要因素。
cues.en: These are two, I think, important pieces of what make it quite high quality and very fast.

cues.zh: 好，MOE [听不清 00:20:22]，输入很大，输出很小。
cues.en: Okay, so MOE [inaudible 00:20:22], the input is huge, the output is small.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那还能说些什么关于如何让……缓存有作用吗——
cues.en: So what else can you say about how to make… Does caching play a role-

cues.zh: 哦，缓存作用巨大。
cues.en: Oh, caching plays a huge role.

cues.zh: 因为你处理这么多输入 token，如果你在某一行里每敲一个键，都得把所有传入的 token 重新跑一遍模型，那首先会大幅增加延迟，其次会让 GPU 负载过高。
cues.en: Because you’re dealing with this many input tokens, if every single keystroke that you’re typing in a given line you had to rerun the model on all of those tokens passed in, you’re just going to one, significantly degrade latency, two, you’re going to kill your GPUs with load.

cues.zh: 所以你需要设计实际给模型用的 prompt，让它们对缓存友好。
cues.en: So you need to design the actual prompts you use for the model such that they’re caching aware.

cues.zh: 然后，是的，你需要在请求之间复用 KV 缓存，这样就能少做工作、少消耗算力。
cues.en: And then yeah, you need to reuse the KV cache across requests just so that you’re spending less work, less compute.

cues.zh: 再问一下，Tab 近期内应该能做到哪些事，就先围绕这一点多聊几句？
cues.en: Again, what are the things that Tab is supposed to be able to do in the near term, just to linger on that?

cues.zh: 生成代码、填充空白，还能跨多行编辑代码，然后跳转到同一文件里的不同位置，接着——
cues.en: Generate code, fill empty space, also edit code across multiple lines and then jump to different locations inside the same file and then-

cues.zh: 希望也能跳转到不同文件。
cues.en: Hopefully jump to different files also.

cues.zh: 所以如果你在一个文件里做了修改，也许还得去另一个文件把思路补完，它也应该能跳到第二个文件去。
cues.en: So if you make an edit in one file and maybe you have to go to another file to finish your thought, it should go to the second file also.

cues.zh: 完整的泛化就是下一个动作预测。
cues.en: The full generalization is next action prediction.

cues.zh: 有时你需要在终端里运行一条命令，它也应该能根据你写的代码来建议命令；有时你其实需要……它给出了建议，但你很难判断对不对，因为你还需要更多信息才能判断。
cues.en: Sometimes you need to run a command in the terminal and it should be able to suggest the command based on the code that you wrote too, or sometimes you actually need to… It suggests something, but it’s hard for you to know if it’s correct because you actually need some more information to learn.

cues.zh: 你得知道类型，才能验证它是否正确。
cues.en: You need to know the type to be able to verify that it’s correct.

cues.zh: 所以也许它应该先把你带到某个东西的定义处，再把你带回来，这样你就有了接受下一次补全所需的全部知识。
cues.en: And so maybe it should actually take you to a place that’s the definition of something and then take you back so that you have all the requisite knowledge to be able to accept the next completion.

cues.zh: 所以就是把知识提供给人类。
cues.en: So providing the human the knowledge.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Right.

cues.zh: 嗯。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我刚认识了一个叫 Primeagen 的人，我相信他有个……你可以通过 SSH 点咖啡。
cues.en: I just gotten to know a guy named Primeagen who I believe has an… You can order coffee via SSH.

cues.zh: 哦对。
cues.en: Oh yeah.

cues.zh: 我们干过那事。
cues.en: We did that.

cues.zh: 我们干过那事。
cues.en: We did that.

cues.zh: 那模型也能这么做，给你提供咖啡因吗？
cues.en: So can also the model do that and provide you with caffeine?

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 这就是整体框架。
cues.en: So that’s the general framework.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 而神奇的时刻会是……编程是一门奇怪的学科，有时接下来五分钟你要做的事——不总是，但有时——其实可以从你最近做过的事情中预测出来。
cues.en: And the magic moment would be if… Programming is this weird discipline where sometimes the next five minutes, not always, but sometimes the next five minutes of what you’re going to do is actually predictable from the stuff you’ve done recently.

cues.zh: 这样你就能进入一个状态：接下来的五分钟要么是你主动退出，让它带你走一遍？
cues.en: And so can you get to a world where that next five minutes either happens by you disengaging and it taking you through?

cues.zh: 或者更多是你看到下一步它会做什么，然后你说，好，不错，不错，不错，不错，你就可以这样点、点、点过这些大改动。
cues.en: Or maybe a little bit more of just you seeing next step what it’s going to do and you’re like, okay, that’s good, that’s good, that’s good, that’s good, and you can just sort of tap, tap through these big changes.

cues.zh: 说到这个，我得提一下 Cursor 一个非常酷且显眼的特点，就是它有整套 diff 界面机制。
cues.en: As we’re talking about this, I should mention one of the really cool and noticeable things about Cursor is that there’s this whole diff interface situation going on.

cues.zh: 模型会用红色和绿色提示这里我们要怎么改代码，在聊天窗口里你可以应用，它会展示 diff，你可以接受这个 diff。
cues.en: So the model suggests with the red and the green of here’s how we’re going to modify the code, and in the chat window you can apply and it shows you the diff and you can accept the diff.

cues.zh: 所以也许你能谈谈这方面的发展方向？
cues.en: So maybe can you speak to whatever direction of that?

cues.zh: 我们大概会有四五种不同的 diff。
cues.en: We’ll probably have four or five different kinds of diffs.

cues.zh: 所以我们针对自动补全优化了 diff，它的 diff 界面和你审查大块代码时不一样。
cues.en: So we have optimized the diff for the auto complete, so that has a different diff interface than when you’re reviewing larger blocks of code.

cues.zh: 然后我们还在试着优化另一种 diff，用于处理多个不同文件的情况。
cues.en: And then we’re trying to optimize another diff thing for when you’re doing multiple different files.

cues.zh: Cursor 的核心运作方式，是靠一组我们自训练的定制模型，配合那些擅长高强度推理的前沿模型。
cues.en: Where Cursor really works via this ensemble of custom models that we’ve trained alongside the frontier models that are fantastic at the reasoning intense things.

cues.zh: 另一个领域是 Apply，它居然需要定制模型，这挺让人意外的，但确实必要，而且效果相当不错。

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这些模型……前沿模型很擅长为代码勾勒方案、生成改动的粗略草图，但真正生成 diff 对前沿模型、对你训练的模型来说都相当难。
cues.en: So I think these models are… The frontier models are quite good at sketching out plans for code and generating rough sketches of the change, but actually, creating diffs is quite hard for frontier models, for your training models.

cues.zh: 你用 Sonnet、o1 或任何前沿模型去试，它真的会在数行号这种蠢事上出错，尤其是在超大文件里。
cues.en: You try to do this with Sonnet, with o1, any frontier model and it really messes up stupid things like counting line numbers, especially in super, super large files.

cues.zh: 所以我们为了缓解这个问题，让模型先勾勒出这个粗略的代码块，表明改动会是什么，然后训练一个模型把这个改动应用到文件里。
cues.en: And so what we’ve done to alleviate this is we let the model sketch out this rough code block that indicates what the change will be and we train a model to then Apply that change to the file.

cues.zh: 我们得说，Apply 就是让模型看你的代码，然后给你一个非常棒的建议，告诉你该做哪些新事情。
cues.en: And we should say that Apply is the model looks at your code, it gives you a really damn good suggestion of what new things to do.

cues.zh: 而把这两者结合起来，对人类来说看似微不足道的一步，你说其实并不那么简单。
cues.en: And the seemingly for humans trivial step of combining the two, you’re saying is not so trivial.

cues.zh: 与普遍认知相反，它并不是一个确定性算法。
cues.en: Contrary to popular perception, it is not a deterministic algorithm.

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得你在别处看到的 Apply 都是浅层复制，大多数时候都会出问题，因为你以为自己能做一些确定性匹配，结果至少有 40% 的概率会失败，这就会导致糟糕的产品体验。
cues.en: Yeah, I think you see shallow copies of apply elsewhere and it just breaks most of the time because you think you can try to do some deterministic matching and then it fails at least 40% of the time and that just results in a terrible product experience.

cues.zh: 我觉得总的来说，这个趋势就是模型会越来越聪明。
cues.en: I think in general, this regime of you are going to get smarter and smarter models.

cues.zh: 所以 Apply 还让你能做到另一件事，就是配合最智能的模型使用更少的 token。
cues.en: So one other thing that Apply lets you do is it lets you use fewer tokens with the most intelligent models.

cues.zh: 生成所有这些 token 在延迟和成本上都很昂贵。
cues.en: This is both expensive in terms of latency for generating all these tokens and cost.

cues.zh: 所以你可以给出这个非常非常粗略的草图，然后让你的模型去实现它，因为实现这种非常非常粗略的代码要容易得多。
cues.en: So you can give this very, very rough sketch and then have your model models go and implement it because it’s a much easier task to implement this very, very sketched out code.

cues.zh: 我认为这种模式会持续下去：你可以用越来越聪明的模型来做规划，然后也许实现细节可以交给不那么聪明的模型来处理。
cues.en: And I think that this regime will continue where you can use smarter and smarter models to do the planning and then maybe the implementation details can be handled by the less intelligent ones.

cues.zh: 也许你会有 o1，也许会有能力更强的模型，给定一个更高层次的计划，由 sauna 和 apply 模型递归地应用。
cues.en: Perhaps you’ll have maybe o1, maybe it’ll be even more capable models given an even higher level plan that is recursively applied by sauna and then the apply model.

cues.zh: 如果你愿意，也许我们应该谈谈如何让它变快。
cues.en: Maybe we should talk about how to make it fast if you like.

cues.zh: 快始终是个有趣的细节。
cues.en: Fast is always an interesting detail.

cues.en: Fast is good.

cues.zh: 那怎么让它变快呢？
cues.en: Yeah, how do you make it fast?

cues.zh: 让速度快的一个重要组成部分是推测性编辑。
cues.en: Yeah, so one big component of making it fast is speculative edits.

cues.zh: 推测性编辑是推测性解码的一种变体，也许简要介绍一下推测性解码会有帮助。
cues.en: So speculative edits are a variant of speculative decoding, and maybe it’d be helpful to briefly describe speculative decoding.

cues.zh: 在推测性解码中，你可以利用这样一个事实：大多数时候——我要补充一个前提，那就是在语言模型生成受内存限制时——如果你一次处理多个token，会比一次生成一个token更快。
cues.en: With speculative decoding, what you do is you can take advantage of the fact that most of the time, and I’ll add the caveat that it would be when you’re memory bound in language model generation, if you process multiple tokens at once, it is faster than generating one token at a time.

cues.zh: 这也是为什么如果你看每秒token数，提示token和生成token相比，提示token要快得多。
cues.en: So this is the same reason why if you look at tokens per second with prompt tokens versus generated tokens, it’s much much faster for prompt tokens.

cues.zh: 所以我们做的不是推测性解码通常做的事——即用一个小模型来预测这些草稿token，然后让更大的模型去验证——在代码编辑中，我们对现有代码的样子有非常强的先验，而这个先验就是完全相同的代码本身。
cues.en: So what we do is instead of using what speculative decoding normally does, which is using a really small model to predict these draft tokens that your larger model will then go in and verify, with code edits, we have a very strong prior of what the existing code will look like and that prior is literally the same exact code.

cues.zh: 你可以把原始代码分块喂回模型，大多数时候模型都会认同，“好，我就把这段代码原样吐出来。”于是你可以并行处理所有这些行，只要分块足够多就能这么做。
cues.en: So you can do is you can just feed chunks of the original code back into the model, and then the model will just pretty much agree most of the time that, “Okay, I’m just going to spit this code back out.” And so you can process all of those lines in parallel and you just do this with sufficiently many chunks.

cues.zh: 最终你会遇到一个分歧点，模型此时预测的文本与原始代码的真实值不同。
cues.en: And then eventually you’ll reach a point of disagreement where the model will now predict text that is different from the ground truth original code.

cues.zh: 它会生成这些 token，然后在足够多的 token 与原始代码匹配之后，我们再决定重新开始按代码块进行推测。
cues.en: It’ll generate those tokens and then we will decide after enough tokens match the original code to re- start speculating in chunks of code.

cues.zh: 实际效果看起来就像是正常编辑代码的加速版。
cues.en: What this actually ends up looking like is just a much faster version of normal editing code.

cues.zh: 所以它看起来就像是模型重写所有代码的加速版。
cues.en: So it looks like a much faster version of the model rewriting all the code.

cues.zh: 所以我们可以用和 diff 完全相同的接口，只是流式传输会快得多。
cues.en: So we can use the same exact interface that we use for diffs, but it will just stream down a lot faster.

cues.zh: 好处是，在流式输出的同时，你就能开始审查代码，不用等一个大加载界面。
cues.en: And then the advantage is that while it’s streaming, you can just also start reviewing the code before it’s done so there’s no big loading screen.

cues.zh: 也许这也算优势之一。
cues.en: Maybe that is part of the advantage.

cues.zh: 所以人可以在东西还没生成完时就开始读。
cues.en: So the human can start reading before the thing is done.

cues.zh: 我觉得这里有意思的点是……我感觉推测如今是个挺常见的概念。
cues.en: I think the interesting riff here is something like… I feel like speculation is a fairly common idea nowadays.

cues.zh: 不只是语言模型里有。
cues.en: It’s not only in language models.

cues.zh: CPU 里显然有推测执行，数据库里也有推测，到处都有推测。
cues.en: There’s obviously speculation in CPUs and there’s speculation for databases and there’s speculation all over the place.

cues.zh: 那我来问个荒唐的问题：哪个 LLM 更擅长写代码？
cues.en: Well, let me ask the ridiculous question of which LLM is better at coding?

cues.zh: GPT、Claude，在编程场景下谁赢？
cues.en: GPT, Claude, who wins in the context of programming?

cues.zh: 我确信答案要微妙得多，因为听起来每一部分都涉及不同的模型。
cues.en: And I’m sure the answer is much more nuanced because it sounds like every single part of this involves a different model.

cues.zh: 我认为没有哪个模型能在所有我们认为重要的维度上全面占优，这些维度包括速度、编辑代码的能力、处理大量代码的能力、长上下文，还有几个其他方面以及编码能力。
cues.en: I think there’s no model that Pareto dominates others, meaning it is better in all categories that we think matter, the categories being speed, ability to edit code, ability to process lots of code, long context, a couple of other things and coding capabilities.

cues.zh: 目前我会说综合表现最好的就是 Sonnet。
cues.en: The one that I’d say right now is just net best is Sonnet.

cues.zh: 我认为这是共识。
cues.en: I think this is a consensus opinion.

cues.zh: o1 非常有意思，它真的很擅长推理。
cues.en: o1’s really interesting and it’s really good at reasoning.

cues.zh: 所以如果你给它很难的编程面试题或 LeetCode 题，它能做得相当好，但它对你想法的理解不如 Sonnet 到位。
cues.en: So if you give it really hard programming interview style problems or lead code problems, it can do quite well on them, but it doesn’t feel like it understands your rough intent as well as Sonnet does.

cues.zh: 如果你看过很多其他前沿模型，我的一点疑虑是，感觉它们未必过于……我不是说它们在基准测试上训练，但它们在基准测试中的表现相对于中间的一切来说实在太好了。
cues.en: If you look at a lot of the other frontier models, one qualm I have is it feels like they’re not necessarily over… I’m not saying they train on benchmarks, but they perform really well in benchmarks relative to everything that’s in the middle.

cues.zh: 所以如果你在这些基准测试以及它们被评估的基准测试分布内的所有东西上测试，它们会表现得非常好。
cues.en: So if you tried on all these benchmarks and things that are in the distribution of the benchmarks they’re evaluated on, they’ll do really well.

cues.zh: 但当你把它们稍微推到那个范围之外时，我认为 Sonnet 是保持同样能力做得最好的那个。
cues.en: But when you push them a little bit outside of that, Sonnet is I think the one that does best at maintaining that same capability.

cues.zh: 你在基准测试中拥有的能力，和你尝试指示它做任何编码任务时的能力是一样的。
cues.en: You have the same capability in the benchmark as when you try to instruct it to do anything with coding.

cues.zh: 另一个荒谬的问题是，正常的编程体验与基准测试所代表的东西之间的差异？
cues.en: Another ridiculous question is the difference between the normal programming experience versus what benchmarks represent?

cues.zh: 你觉得在评估这些模型时，基准测试哪里不够用？
cues.en: Where do benchmarks fall short, do you think, when we’re evaluating these models?

cues.zh: 顺便说，基准测试和真实编程之间的差异，是一个非常非常难、又极其关键的细节，真实编程可不是面试风格的编程。
cues.en: By the way, that’s a really, really hard, critically important detail of how different benchmarks are versus real coding, where real coding, it’s not interview style coding.

cues.zh: 人类有时说的是半吊子英语，有时你说“按我之前做的来”，有时你说“去加这个东西，然后帮我做另一件事，再做这个 UI 元素”。很多事情都依赖上下文。
cues.en: Humans are saying half-broken English sometimes and sometimes you’re saying, “Oh, do what I did before.” Sometimes you’re saying, “Go add this thing and then do this other thing for me and then make this UI element.” And then it’s just a lot of things are context dependent.

cues.zh: 你真正想要的是理解人，然后做人想要的事，而不是这种……也许抽象地说，面试题是定义得非常明确的。
cues.en: You really want to understand the human and then do what the human wants, as opposed to this… Maybe the way to put it abstractly is the interview problems are very well specified.

cues.zh: 他们很依赖规范说明，而人类那部分则规范得比较少。
cues.en: They lean a lot on specification while the human stuff is less specified.

cues.zh: 我觉得这个基准测试问题既因为 Sualeh 刚才提到的内容而变得复杂，也因为 Aman 正在探讨的一点，那就是即便你……这里存在一个问题，就是基准测试中能建模的东西与真实编程之间存在偏差，而这有时很难被封装起来，因为真实编程非常混乱，有时候对于什么是对的、什么是不对的，并没有特别明确的规范。
cues.en: I think that this benchmark question is both complicated by what Sualeh just mentioned, and then also what Aman was getting into is that even if you… There’s this problem of the skew between what can you actually model in a benchmark versus real programming, and that can be sometimes hard to encapsulate because it’s real programming’s very messy and sometimes things aren’t super well specified what’s correct or what isn’t.

cues.zh: 但接着又因为公开基准测试的问题而变得难上加难。
cues.en: But then it’s also doubly hard because of this public benchmark problem.

cues.zh: 这既是因为公开基准测试有时会被用来刷榜，也是因为很难把公开基准测试的数据从模型中提取出来。
cues.en: And that’s both because public benchmarks are sometimes hill climbed on, then it’s really, really hard to also get the data from the public benchmarks out of the models.

cues.zh: 比如说，最流行的智能体基准测试之一 SWE-Bench，在这些基础模型的训练数据里其实污染得非常严重。
cues.en: And so for instance, one of the most popular agent benchmarks, SWE-Bench, is really, really contaminated in the training data of these foundation models.

cues.zh: 所以如果你让这些基础模型去做 SWE-Bench 的题目，但又不给它代码库的上下文，它就能凭空编出正确的文件路径，编出正确的函数名。
cues.en: And so if you ask these foundation models to do a SWE-Bench problem, but you actually don’t give them the context of a code base, they can hallucinate the right file pass, they can hallucinate the right function names.

cues.zh: 而且这些东西公开出来本身也很麻烦。
cues.en: And so it’s also just the public aspect of these things is tricky.

cues.zh: 那种情况下，它可能直接拿真实的 issue 或 pull request 来训练，也许实验室会开始做得更好，或者他们已经在去污染方面做得不错了，但他们不会把仓库本身的真实训练数据去掉。
cues.en: In that case, it could be trained on the literal issues or pull requests themselves, and maybe the labs will start to do a better job or they’ve already done a good job at decontaminating those things, but they’re not going to omit the actual training data of the repository itself.

cues.zh: 这些都是最受欢迎的 Python 仓库。
cues.en: These are all some of the most popular Python repositories.

cues.zh: SimPy 就是一个例子。
cues.en: SimPy is one example.

cues.zh: 我不认为他们会为了在这些基准测试中拿到真实评分，就在 SimPy 和所有这些热门 Python 仓库上削弱自己的模型。
cues.en: I don’t think they’re going to handicap their models on SimPy and all these popular Python repositories in order to get true evaluation scores in these benchmarks.

cues.zh: 我觉得，鉴于基准测试里的那些猫腻，用这些模型构建系统或构建这些模型的地方，确实会用一些有意思的拐杖，来判断自己是不是走在正确的方向上。
cues.en: I think that given the dirts in benchmarks, there have been a few interesting crutches that places that build systems with these models or build these models actually use to get a sense of are they going the right direction or not.

cues.zh: 在很多地方，人们实际上就是让人来玩这些东西，给出定性反馈。
cues.en: And in a lot of places, people will actually just have humans play with the things and give qualitative feedback on these.

cues.zh: 有一两家基础模型公司，有人的主要职责就是做这个。
cues.en: One or two of the foundation model companies, they have people who that’s a big part of their role.

cues.zh: 在内部，我们也会对这些模型做定性评估，而且除了我们有的私有邮件之外，很大程度上也依赖这个。
cues.en: And internally, we also qualitatively assess these models and actually lean on that a lot in addition to private emails that we have.

cues.zh: 这就像那种感觉。
cues.en: It’s like the vibe.

cues.zh: 那种感觉，对，就是那种感觉。
cues.en: The vibe, yeah, the vibe.

cues.zh: 这就像那种感觉。
cues.en: It’s like the vibe.

cues.zh: 那种感觉基准，人类基准，就是人类。
cues.en: The vibe benchmark, human benchmark, the humans.

cues.zh: 你拉来人类做感觉检查。
cues.en: You pull in the humans to do a vibe check.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 我就是这么做的。
cues.en: That’s what I do.

cues.zh: 就是看看在线论坛、Reddit 和 X 上的讨论。
cues.en: Just reading online forums and Reddit and X.

cues.zh: 我不知道该怎么正确加载人们的意见，因为他们会说“我感觉 Claude 或 GPT 变笨了”之类的话。
cues.en: Well, I don’t know how to properly load in people’s opinions because they’ll say things like, “I feel like Claude or GPT has gotten dumber,” or something.

cues.zh: 他们会说“我感觉……”，然后我有时也有同感，但我不知道是模型的问题还是我的问题。
cues.en: They’ll say, “I feel like…” And then I sometimes feel like that too, but I wonder if it’s the model’s problem or mine.

cues.zh: 关于 Claude，我听过一个有意思的说法：我觉得 AWS 有不同的芯片，我怀疑它们的数值精度和 Nvidia GPU 略有不同，有人推测 Claude 性能下降可能跟用的是 AWS Bedrock 上的量化版本，而不是 Anthropic GPU 上跑的那个版本有关。
cues.en: With Claude, there’s an interesting take I heard where I think AWS has different chips and I suspect they have slightly different numerics than Nvidia GPUs, and someone speculated that Claude’s degraded performance had to do with maybe using the quantized version that existed on AWS Bedrock versus whatever was running on Anthropics GPUs.

cues.zh: 我采访过一些相信阴谋论的人。
cues.en: I interview a bunch of people that have conspiracy theories.

cues.zh: 很高兴你和这个阴谋论聊过。
cues.en: I’m glad you spoke to this conspiracy.

cues.zh: 嗯，与其说是阴谋论，不如说是关于人类的。
cues.en: Well, it’s not like conspiracy theory as much as humans.

cues.zh: 人类就是人类，总有这些细节——
cues.en: Humans are humans and there’s these details-

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 你做的这些让人不安的大量浮点运算和芯片一团糟，老兄，你只会遇到bug。
cues.en: And you’re doing this queasy amount of flops and chips are messy and man, you can just have bugs.

cues.zh: 很难夸大避免bug有多难。
cues.en: It’s hard to overstate how hard bugs are to avoid.

cues.zh: 在这一切中，好的提示词起什么作用？
cues.en: What’s the role of a good prompt in all of this?

cues.zh: 我们提到过，基准测试有非常结构化、精心设计的提示词。
cues.en: We mentioned that benchmarks have really structured, well-formulated prompts.

cues.zh: 人类应该怎么做才能最大化成功率，人类的重要性体现在哪里……你写了一篇博客文章……你称之为提示词设计。
cues.en: What should a human be doing to maximize success and what’s the importance of what the humans… You wrote a blog post on… You called it Prompt Design.

cues.zh: 是的，我觉得这取决于你用哪个模型，它们都略有不同，对不同提示词的反应也不同，但我认为最初的GPT-4和去年最初的[听不清 00:44:07]模型，它们对提示词相当敏感，而且上下文窗口也非常小。
cues.en: Yeah, I think it depends on which model you’re using, and all of them are slightly different and they respond differently to different prompts, but I think the original GPT-4 and the original [inaudible 00:44:07] models last year, they were quite sensitive to the prompts, and they also had a very small context window.

cues.zh: 所以代码库周围有所有这些信息，它们可能跟提示词相关。
cues.en: And so we have all of these pieces of information around the code base that would maybe be relevant in the prompt.

cues.zh: 你有文档、添加的文件、对话历史，然后问题就来了：你怎么决定实际放进提示词的内容，尤其是在空间有限的时候？
cues.en: You have the docs, you have the files that you add, you have the conversation history, and then there’s a problem like how do you decide what you actually put in the prompt and when you have a limited space?

cues.zh: 即便对今天的模型来说，即使有长上下文，填满整个上下文窗口也意味着速度更慢。
cues.en: And even for today’s models, even when you have long context, filling out the entire context window means that it’s slower.

cues.zh: 这意味着模型有时会真的搞混，而且有些模型比其他模型更容易混淆。
cues.en: It means that sometimes the model actually gets confused and some models get more confused than others.

cues.zh: 我们内部有一个叫 Preempt 的系统，能帮我们稍微缓解这个问题。
cues.en: And we have this one system internally that we call Preempt, which helps us with that a little bit.

cues.zh: 我觉得它是在我们只有 8000 token 上下文窗口的时代构建的。
cues.en: And I think it was built for the era before where we had 8,000 token contact windows.

cues.zh: 这和做网站有点类似。
cues.en: And it’s a little bit similar to when you’re making a website.

cues.zh: 你希望它在手机上能用，在桌面屏幕上也能用，而且你手头有这些动态信息，这是你原本没有的。
cues.en: You want it to work on mobile, you want it to work on a desktop screen, and you have this dynamic information which you don’t have.

cues.zh: 比如设计印刷杂志时，你很清楚东西该放在哪。
cues.en: For example, if you’re designing a print magazine, you know exactly where you can put stuff.

cues.zh: 但做网站或写提示词时，你有这些输入，然后需要把它们格式化得始终能用，即使输入非常大，也可能得裁掉一些内容。
cues.en: But when you have a website or when you have a prompt, you have these inputs and then you need to format them to always work, even if the input is really big, then you might have to cut something down.

cues.zh: 所以想法是，好，我们借鉴一些灵感。
cues.en: And so the idea was, okay, let’s take some inspiration.

cues.zh: 设计网站的最佳方式是什么？
cues.en: What’s the best way to design websites?

cues.zh: 我们真正喜欢的是 React 和声明式方法，在 JavaScript 里用 JSX，然后你声明：“这就是我想要的，我认为这个优先级更高，或者这个的 Z 轴索引比其他高。”
cues.en: Well, the thing that we really like is React and the declarative approach where you use JSX in JavaScript, and then you declare, “This is what I want and I think this has higher priority or this has higher Z index than something else.”

cues.zh: 然后网页设计里就有这个渲染引擎。
cues.en: And then you have this rendering engine in web design.

cues.zh: 这就像 Chrome，在我们的场景里是一个抢占式渲染器，它会把所有内容适配到页面上。
cues.en: It’s like Chrome, and in our case it’s a preempt renderer, which then fits everything onto the page.

cues.zh: 你只需声明、决定你想要什么，然后它就会弄清楚你想要什么。
cues.en: And as you declare, decide what you want and then it figures out what you want.

cues.zh: 我们发现这非常有用，而且我认为它的角色随着时间发生了变化，最初是为了适配这些小上下文窗口。
cues.en: And so we have found that to be quite helpful and I think the role of it has shifted over time where initially it was to fit to these small context windows.

cues.zh: 现在它真的很有用，因为它帮我们拆分进入提示词的数据以及实际渲染。
cues.en: Now it’s really useful because it helps us with splitting up the data that goes into the prompt and the actual rendering of it.

cues.zh: 这样调试更容易，因为你可以修改提示词的渲染方式，然后在旧提示词上试，因为你有进入提示词的原始数据，然后你能看到：“我的改动是否真的在整个评估集上改善了效果？”
cues.en: And so it’s easier to debug because you can change the rendering of the prompt and then try it on old prompts because you have the raw data that went into the prompt, and then you can see, “Did my change actually improve it for this entire eval set?”

cues.zh: 所以你真的用 JSX 来写提示词吗？
cues.en: So do you literally prompt with JSX?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 所以它看起来像 React。
cues.en: So it looks like react.

cues.zh: 有组件。
cues.en: There are components.

cues.zh: 我们有一个组件是文件组件，它接收光标。
cues.en: We have one component that’s a file component and it takes in the cursor.

cues.zh: 通常文件里光标所在的那一行只有一行，而那大概是最重要的一行，因为那是你正在看的那一行。
cues.en: Usually there’s one line where the cursor is in your file and that’s probably the most important line because that’s the one you’re looking at.

cues.zh: 然后你就可以给它们设定优先级。
cues.en: And so then you can give priorities.

cues.zh: 所以那一行优先级最高，然后每远离一行就减一。
cues.en: So that line has the highest priority, and then you subtract one for every line that is farther away.

cues.zh: 最后渲染的时候，它会算出实际能放下多少行，并以那个位置为中心。
cues.en: And then eventually when it’s rendered, it figures out how many lines can actually fit and it centers around that thing.

cues.zh: 太厉害了。
cues.en: That’s amazing.

cues.zh: 你还能做其他花哨的事，比如如果你有来自整个代码库的大量代码块，你可以用检索，以及嵌入和重排序分数之类的方法，通过这些组件为你添加优先级。
cues.en: And you can do other fancy things where if you have lots of code blocks from the entire code base, you could use retrieval and things like embedding and re-ranking scores to add priorities for you through these components.

cues.zh: 那么人类在提问时，是不是也应该尝试用类似的方式？
cues.en: So should humans when they ask questions, also try to use something like that?

cues.zh: 在问题里写 JSX 会有帮助吗，还是说整个理念就是应该松散、随意？
cues.en: Would it be beneficial to write JSX in the problem or the whole idea is this should be loose and messy?

cues.zh: 我觉得我们的目标是，你就按对你来说最自然的方式去做，然后我们的工作是搞清楚如何真正检索到相关的事件信息，让你的思考真正说得通？
cues.en: I think our goal is that you should just do whatever is the most natural thing for you, and then our job is to figure out how do we actually retrieve the relative event things so that your thinking actually makes sense?

cues.zh: 嗯，这就是我和 Perplexity 的 Aravind 讨论过的，他的整个理念就是应该让人想多懒就多懒。
cues.en: Well, this is the discussion I had with Aravind of Perplexity is his whole idea is you should let the person be as lazy as he wants.

cues.zh: 这很美好，但我觉得你可以对程序员提出更高的要求，对吧？
cues.en: That’s a beautiful thing, but I feel like you’re allowed to ask more of programmers, right?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 所以如果你说“想怎么做就怎么做”，人类是会偷懒的。
cues.en: So if you say, “Just do what you want,” humans are lazy.

cues.zh: 在单纯偷懒和提供更多信息、被提示之间存在着一种张力……几乎就像是系统在给你压力，或者激励你表达得更清楚。
cues.en: There’s a tension between just being lazy versus provide more as be prompted… Almost like the system pressuring you or inspiring you to be articulate.

cues.zh: 不是从句子语法层面，而是从你在提示词里传达的思想深度来看。
cues.en: Not in terms of the grammar of the sentences, but in terms of the depth of thoughts that you convey inside the prompts.

cues.zh: 我认为，即使系统越来越接近某种完美程度，当你向模型提出请求时，往往也没有传达足够的意图，让它知道该怎么做。
cues.en: I think even as a system gets closer to some level of perfection, often when you ask the model for something, not enough intent is conveyed to know what to do.

cues.zh: 要解决意图问题，有几种方法。
cues.en: And there are a few ways to resolve that intent.

cues.zh: 一种是简单做法，让模型直接问你：“根据你的查询，我不确定这些部分该怎么做。
cues.en: One is the simple thing of having the model just ask you, “I’m not sure how to do these parts based on your query.

cues.zh: 你能澄清一下吗？”另一种可能是，如果有五六个可能的生成结果，“鉴于你的查询目前存在不确定性，为什么不干脆把所有这些都展示给你，让你自己选？”
cues.en: Could you clarify that?” I think the other could be maybe if there are five or six possible generations, “Given the uncertainty present in your query so far, why don’t we just actually show you all of those and let you pick them?”

cues.zh: 模型选择反问而不是一般性回应，有多难？很难，难在如何处理不确定性。
cues.en: How hard is it for the model to choose to talk back versus generally… It’s hard, how deal with the uncertainty.

cues.zh: 我会选择询问更多信息来减少歧义吗？
cues.en: Do I choose to ask for more information to reduce the ambiguity?

cues.zh: 我们最近新增的一个功能，是尝试推荐你可以添加的文件。
cues.en: So one of the things we do, it’s like a recent addition, is try to suggest files that you can add.

cues.zh: 在你输入时，可以推测不确定点在哪里，也许能猜到你正在写 API，并且可以通过你在同一文件中之前的提交来推测客户端和服务端非常有用，而如何跨所有提交解决这个问题是一个艰难的技术难题。
cues.en: And while you’re typing, one can guess what the uncertainty is and maybe suggest that maybe you’re writing your API and we can guess using the commits that you’ve made previously in the same file that the client and the server is super useful and there’s a hard technical problem of how do you resolve it across all commits?

cues.zh: 根据你当前的提示，哪些文件最重要？
cues.en: Which files are the most important given your current prompt?

cues.zh: 初始版本仍被排除在外，我相信我们可以让它准确得多。
cues.en: And we’re still initial version is ruled out and I’m sure we can make it much more accurate.

cues.zh: 这非常实验性，但思路是向你展示，你是否只想添加这个文件、这个文件、这个文件，也让模型为你编辑这些文件？
cues.en: It’s very experimental, but then the idea is we show you, do you just want to add this file, this file, this file also to tell the model to edit those files for you?

cues.zh: 因为如果你在开发 API，那也应该同时修改使用这个 API 的客户端和服务端，以及另一端解析这个 API 的部分。
cues.en: Because if maybe you’re making the API, you should also edit the client and the server that is using the API and the other one resolving the API.

cues.zh: 所以那样会很酷，因为既有你写提示词的阶段，也有……在你甚至还没点“回车”之前，也许我们能帮忙消除一些不确定性。
cues.en: So that would be cool as both there’s the phase where you’re writing a prompt and there’s… Before you even click, “Enter,” maybe we can help resolve some of the uncertainty.

cues.en: Okay.

cues.en: And so I think there are certain types of tasks where having an agent would be really nice.

cues.zh: 我很想有个智能体。
cues.en: I would love to have an agent.

cues.zh: 你是说它会自己去找对应的文件？
cues.en: You mean it goes, finds the right file?

cues.zh: 对，它找到对应的文件，尝试复现 bug，修好它，然后验证是否正确。
cues.en: Yeah, it finds the right files, it tries to reproduce the bug, it fixes the bug and then it verifies that it’s correct.

cues.zh: 这个过程可能耗时很长。
cues.en: And this could be a process that takes a long time.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得我会很想要这个。
cues.en: And so I think I would love to have that.

cues.zh: 然后我觉得，在很多编程工作中，人们常常有一种信念，认为智能体会接管所有的编程工作。
cues.en: And then I think a lot of programming, there is often this belief that agents will take over all of programming.

cues.zh: 我不认为我们会这样看，因为很多编程工作的价值在于迭代，或者你其实并不想一开始就明确指定某些东西，因为在你看到初始版本之前，你并不真正知道自己想要什么，然后你想在此基础上迭代，再提供更多信息。

cues.zh: 所以对于很多编程工作，我认为你其实想要一个即时响应的系统，能立刻给你一个初始版本，然后你可以超快地迭代。
cues.en: And so for a lot of programming, I think you actually want a system that’s instant, that gives you an initial version instantly back and then you can iterate super, super quickly.

cues.zh: 最近出现的类似的东西，比如replica agent，它还会搭建开发环境、解决软件包问题、配置所有东西、配置数据库，并实际部署应用，那这个怎么样？
cues.en: What about something like that recently came out, replica agent, that does also setting up the development environment and solving software packages, configuring everything, configuring the databases and actually deploying the app.

cues.zh: 这也是你梦想中的一部分吗？
cues.en: Is that also in the set of things you dream about?
