cues.en: I think so.

cues.zh: 我觉得那会非常酷。
cues.en: I think that would be really cool.

cues.zh: 对某些类型的编程来说，那会非常酷。
cues.en: For certain types of programming, it would be really cool.

cues.zh: 这在 Cursor 的范围内吗？
cues.en: Is that within scope of Cursor?

cues.zh: 是的，我们目前没有在积极做这件事，但这绝对是……我们想让程序员的生活更轻松、更有趣，有些事就是很繁琐，你需要经过一堆步骤，你想把那些委托给一个 agent。
cues.en: Yeah, we aren’t actively working on it right now, but it’s definitely… We want to make the programmer’s life easier and more fun and some things are just really tedious and you need to go through a bunch of steps and you want to delegate that to an agent.

cues.zh: 然后有些事你其实可以在工作时让一个 agent 在后台处理。
cues.en: And then some things you can actually have an agent in the background while you’re working.

cues.zh: 比如说你有一个 PR，既有后端又有前端，你在做前端，然后你可以让一个后台 agent 不干活，去搞清楚你在做什么。
cues.en: Let’s say you have a PR that’s both backend and frontend, and you’re working in the frontend and then you can have a background agent that doesn’t work and figure out what you’re doing.

cues.zh: 然后当你做到 PR 的后端部分时，你就有了一些初始代码，可以在此基础上迭代。
cues.en: And then when you get to the backend part of your PR, then you have some initial piece of code that you can iterate on.

cues.zh: 所以那也会非常酷。
cues.en: And so that would also be really cool.

cues.zh: 我们已经谈过的一点是速度，但我想我们能不能再多聊聊这个，聊聊让这个东西真正变快的各个技术细节所在的地方。
cues.en: One of the things we already talked about is speed, but I wonder if we can just linger on that some more in the various places that the technical details involved in making this thing really fast.

cues.zh: 所以 Cursor 的每一个方面，Cursor 的大多数方面都感觉非常快。
cues.en: So every single aspect of Cursor, most aspects of Cursor feel really fast.

cues.zh: 就像我提到的，Apply 可能是最慢的部分。
cues.en: Like I mentioned, the Apply is probably the slowest thing.

cues.zh: 对我来说从……抱歉，我说这话时 Arvid 脸上的痛苦表情。
cues.en: And for me from… I’m sorry, the pain on Arvid’s face as I say that.

cues.zh: 我知道。
cues.en: I know.

cues.zh: 这很痛苦。
cues.en: It’s a pain.

cues.zh: 这是我们正在感受的痛苦，我们正在努力修复它。
cues.en: It’s a pain that we’re feeling and we’re working on fixing it.

cues.zh: 是啊，它说的是某种感觉……我不知道具体是多少，大概一两秒吧，那感觉就慢了。
cues.en: Yeah, it says something that feels… I don’t know what it is, like one second or two seconds, that feels slow.

cues.zh: 这说明实际上其他所有环节都真的非常快。
cues.en: That means that actually shows that everything else is just really, really fast.

cues.zh: 那么，关于如何制作这些模型、如何让聊天变快、如何让差异计算变快，有没有什么技术细节？
cues.en: So is there some technical details about how to make some of these models, how to make the chat fast, how to make the diffs fast?

cues.zh: 有什么马上想到的吗？
cues.en: Is there something that just jumps to mind?

cues.zh: 有。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我们可以过一遍我们用的很多策略。
cues.en: So we can go over a lot of the strategies that we use.

cues.zh: 一个有意思的点是缓存预热。
cues.en: One interesting thing is cache warming.

cues.zh: 你可以做的是，当用户打字时，你可以……你大概会用到某段上下文，而这一点在用户打完字之前你就能知道。
cues.en: And so what you can do is if as the user’s typing, you can have… You’re probably going to use some piece of context and you can know that before the user’s done typing.

cues.zh: 所以正如我们之前讨论的，复用 KV 缓存能降低延迟、降低成本，跨请求也能受益。
cues.en: So as we discussed before, reusing the KV cache results in lower latency, lower costs, cross requests.

cues.zh: 所以当用户开始打字时，你可以立刻用比如当前文件内容来预热缓存，然后当他们按下回车时，实际需要预填充和计算的 token 就非常少了，之后就能开始生成。
cues.en: So as the user starts typing, you can immediately warm the cache with let’s say the current file contents, and then when they press enter, there’s very few tokens it actually has to pre-fill and compute before starting the generation.

cues.zh: 这会显著降低 TTFT。
cues.en: This will significantly lower TTFT.

cues.zh: 能解释一下 KV cache 是怎么工作的吗？
cues.en: Can you explain how KV cache works?

cues.zh: 好，那就先说说 Transformer 的工作原理。
cues.en: Yeah, so the way transformers work.

cues.zh: 我喜欢这个。
cues.en: I like it.

cues.zh: 让 Transformer 不只是独立地……让 Transformer 不只是独立地看每个 token，而是能看到之前的 token，靠的机制之一就是注意力中的键和值。
cues.en: One of the mechanisms that allow transformers to not just independently… The mechanism that allows transformers to not just independently look at each token, but see previous tokens are the keys and values to attention.

cues.zh: 一般来说，注意力的工作方式是：当前 token 有一个 query，然后你有之前所有 token 的 keys 和 values，这些是模型内部存储的、对 prompt 中所有先前 token 的某种表示。
cues.en: And generally, the way attention works is you have at your current token some query, and then you’ve all the keys and values of all your previous tokens, which are some kind of representation that the model stores internally of all the previous tokens in the prompt.

cues.zh: 默认情况下，做聊天时，模型对每一个 token 都得把整个模型前向跑一遍。
cues.en: And by default, when you’re doing a chat, the model has to, for every single token, do this forward pass through the entire model.

cues.zh: 这涉及大量矩阵乘法，速度真的非常慢。
cues.en: That’s a lot of matrix multiplies that happen, and that is really, really slow.

cues.zh: 相反，如果你已经完成了这些计算，并把键和值存起来、保留在 GPU 上，那么当我……假设我要对最后 N 个 token 做处理。
cues.en: Instead, if you have already done that and you stored the keys and values and you keep that in the GPU, then when I… Let’s say I have to sort it for the last N tokens.

cues.zh: 如果我现在想计算第 N+1 个 token 的输出，我不需要把前 N 个 token 再送进整个模型，因为我已经有了那些键和值。
cues.en: If I now want to compute the output token for the N+1nth token, I don’t need to pass those first N tokens through the entire model because I already have all those keys and values.

cues.zh: 所以你只需要对最后一个 token 做前向传播。
cues.en: And so you just need to do the forward pass through that last token.

cues.zh: 然后在做注意力时，你复用了已经计算好的那些键和值，而这正是 Transformer 中唯一具有顺序依赖性的部分。
cues.en: And then when you’re doing attention, you’re reusing those keys and values that have been computed, which is the only kind of sequential part or sequentially dependent part of the transformer.

cues.zh: 有没有更高层的缓存，比如对提示词做缓存之类的，能有所帮助？
cues.en: Is there higher level caching of caching of the prompts or that kind of stuff that could help?

cues.zh: 我明白了。
cues.en: I see.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 还有其他类型的缓存可以用。
cues.en: There’s other types of caching you can do.

cues.zh: 对 Cursor Tab 来说，有个挺有意思的做法：你可以提前预测，就当用户已经接受了建议，然后触发另一个请求。
cues.en: One interesting thing that you can do for Cursor Tab is you can basically predict ahead as if the user would’ve accepted the suggestion and then trigger another request.

cues.zh: 这样你就缓存好了，做了推测性预取。
cues.en: And so then you’ve cached, you’ve done the speculative.

cues.zh: 这是推测和缓存的结合，对吧？
cues.en: It’s a mix of speculation and caching, right?

cues.zh: 因为是在推测如果他们接受了会发生什么。
cues.en: Because speculating what would happen if they accepted it.

cues.zh: 然后你就有了这个缓存好的建议值。
cues.en: And then you have this value that is cached this suggestion.

cues.zh: 等他们按下 Tab 时，下一条建议已经立刻等着了。
cues.en: And then when they press tab, the next one would be waiting for them immediately.

cues.zh: 这是个巧妙的启发式技巧，用了更高层的缓存，能带来……感觉很快，尽管模型本身其实没有任何变化。
cues.en: It’s a clever heuristic/trick that uses a higher level caching and can give the… It feels fast despite there not actually being any changes in the model.

cues.zh: 而且如果你能把 KV 缓存做得更小，好处之一就是也许能推测得更多。
cues.en: And if you can make the KV cache smaller, one of the advantages you get is like maybe you can speculate even more.

cues.zh: 也许你能猜到，“这10个可能有用，预测接下来的10个”，然后用户可能正好命中这10个中的一个。
cues.en: Maybe you can guess, “Here’s the 10 things that could be useful, predict the next 10,” and then it’s possible the user hits the one of the 10.

cues.zh: 这比用户恰好命中你展示的那一个，概率要高得多。
cues.en: It’s much higher chance than the user hits the exact one that you showed them.

cues.zh: 也许他们输入了其他字符，命中了缓存里的其他内容。
cues.en: Maybe they type in other character and hit something else in the cache.

cues.zh: 所以有这些技巧……这里的普遍现象是，我觉得它对强化学习也超级有用，也许从模型里单个采样效果不太好，但如果你预测10个不同的东西，结果这10个中有一个是对的，概率会高得多。
cues.en: So there’s all these tricks where… The general phenomena here is, I think it’s also super useful for RL is maybe a single sample from the model isn’t very good, but if you predict 10 different things, turns out that one of the 10 that’s right is the probability is much higher.

cues.zh: 有这些被动的K曲线，而强化学习的一部分，强化学习所做的就是你可以利用这种被动的K现象来做出许多不同的预测。
cues.en: There’s these passive K curves and part of RL, what RL does is you can exploit this passive K phenomena to make many different predictions.

cues.zh: 一种理解方式是，模型内部知道对于哪个关键点是正确的、或者人类想要哪个关键点，存在一些不确定性？
cues.en: And one way to think about this, the model knows internally has some uncertainty over which of the key things is correct or which of the key things does the human wants?

cues.zh: 当我们对 Cursor Tab 模型做强化学习时，其中一件事就是预测模型生成的 100 个不同建议中，哪一个更容易被人类接受？
cues.en: When we RL our Cursor Tab model, one of the things we’re doing is we’re predicting which of the 100 different suggestions the model produces is more amenable for humans?

cues.zh: 哪些建议人类比其他建议更喜欢？
cues.en: Which of them do humans more like than other things?

cues.zh: 也许有些情况下模型能预测得很远，有些只能预测一点点，也许有些在中间。
cues.en: Maybe there’s something where the model can predict very far ahead versus a little bit, maybe somewhere in the middle.

cues.zh: 然后你可以给人类更喜欢的那些东西奖励，惩罚它自己喜欢的那些，再训练模型输出人类更喜欢的建议。
cues.en: And then you can give a reward to the things that humans would like more and punish the things that it would like, and then train the model to output the suggestions that humans would like more.

cues.zh: 你有这些强化学习循环，它们非常有用，能利用这些被动的K曲线。
cues.en: You have these RL loops that are very useful that exploit these passive K curves.

cues.zh: Aman，也许可以讲得更详细一些。
cues.en: Aman, maybe can go into even more detail.

cues.zh: 是的，这和速度有点不同，但从技术上讲，你可以把它联系起来，因为如果你对小模型做强化学习，并且它能达到和大模型相同的性能，你就可以用更小的模型来替代。
cues.en: Yeah, it is a little different than speed, but technically, you tie it back in because you can get away with the smaller model if you RL your smaller model and it gets the same performance as the bigger one.

cues.zh: ……和大模型一样。
cues.en: … as the bigger one.

cues.zh: 所以刚才我提到了关于KV的内容，关于减小KV缓存的大小，还有其他技术也非常有助于提升速度。
cues.en: So while I was mentioning stuff about KV, about reducing the size of your KV cache, there are other techniques there as well that are really helpful for speed.

cues.zh: 回到两年前，人们主要使用多头注意力，我认为现在已经转向更高效的注意力方案，比如分组查询或多查询注意力，这对于更大的批量大小能够更快地生成token非常有帮助。
cues.en: So kind of back in the day, all the way two years ago, people mainly use multi-head attention, and I think there’s been a migration towards more efficient attention schemes like group query or multi-query attention, and this is really helpful for then with larger batch sizes being able to generate the tokens much faster.

cues.zh: 有意思的是，这对首 token 预填充速度没有影响。
cues.en: The interesting thing here is this now has no effect on that time to first token pre-fill speed.

cues.zh: 它影响的是生成 token 的阶段。
cues.en: The thing this matters for is now generating tokens.

cues.zh: 为什么呢？
cues.en: And why is that?

cues.zh: 因为生成 token 时，瓶颈不再是跨所有 token 做那些高度可并行的矩阵乘法，而是……对于长上下文和大批量，瓶颈在于读取缓存中 key 和 value 的速度。
cues.en: Because when you’re generating tokens, instead of being bottlenecked by doing these super parallelizable matrix multiplies across all your tokens, you’re bottlenecked by how quickly… For a long context with large batch sizes, by how quickly you can read those cache, keys, and values.

cues.zh: 所以这就受限于内存带宽，那怎么才能加快速度呢？
cues.en: And so then that’s memory bandwidth, and how can we make this faster?

cues.zh: 我们可以尝试压缩这些 key 和 value 的大小。
cues.en: We can try to compress the size of these keys and values.

cues.zh: 多查询注意力是其中最激进的做法。
cues.en: So multi-query attention is the most aggressive of these.

cues.zh: 通常多头注意力里，有一定数量的所谓“注意力头”和一定数量的查询头。
cues.en: Where normally with multi-head attention, you have some number of, quote, unquote, “attention heads” and some number of query heads.

cues.zh: 多查询只是保留查询头，去掉所有键值头。
cues.en: Multi-query just preserves the query heads, gets rid of all the key value heads.

cues.zh: 所以只有一种键值头，剩下的全是查询头。
cues.en: So there’s only one kind of key value head, and there’s all the remaining query heads.

cues.zh: 分组查询则是保留所有查询头，然后键和值……键和值的头更少，但不会缩减到只剩一个。
cues.en: With group query, you instead preserve all the query heads and then your keys and values are… There are fewer heads for the keys and values, but you’re not reducing it to just one.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，核心就是缩小 KV 缓存的大小。
cues.en: But anyways, the whole point here is you’re just reducing the size of your KV cache.

cues.zh: 然后是 MLA。
cues.en: And then there is MLA.

cues.zh: 对，多头潜在注意力。
cues.en: Yeah, multi-latent.

cues.zh: 这个稍微复杂一点。
cues.en: That’s a little more complicated.

cues.zh: 它的工作方式是把所有头上的键和值整体转成一个潜在向量，然后再按时间展开。
cues.en: And the way that this works is it kind of turns the entirety of your keys and values across all your heads into this one latent vector that has then kind of expanded in for its time.

cues.zh: 但 MLA 来自一家叫 DeepSeek 的公司。
cues.en: But MLA is from this company called DeepSeek.

cues.zh: 这是个挺有意思的算法。
cues.en: It’s quite an interesting algorithm.

cues.zh: 关键思路可能在于MQA以及其他地方，你要做的就是减少KV头的数量。
cues.en: Maybe the key idea is in both MQA and in other places, what you’re doing is you’re reducing the number of KV heads.

cues.zh: 好处是KV头变少了，但理论可能是你其实想要很多不同的……你希望每个key和value都各不相同。
cues.en: And the advantage you get from that is there’s less of them, but maybe the theory is that you actually want a lot of different… You want each of the keys and values to actually be different.

cues.zh: 所以减小规模的一种方法是，为所有key和value保留一个大共享向量，然后为每个token保留更小的向量。
cues.en: So one way to reduce the size is you keep one big shared vector for all the keys and values and then you have smaller vectors for every single token.

cues.zh: 这样你只需存储更小的东西，作为某种低秩压缩，而低秩压缩嘛，最终当你想要计算最终结果时，记住你的内存带宽，这意味着你还有剩余算力可以用在这些事情上。
cues.en: So that you can store the only the smaller thing as some sort of low-rank reduction, and the low-rank reduction, well, that… At the end of the time, when you eventually want to compute the final thing, remember that your memory band, which means that you still have some compute left that you can use for these things.

cues.zh: 如果你能把潜在向量展开回去，而且这在某种程度上效率高得多，因为你在缩减……比如，你可能把 vec 32 之类的向量大小缩减了，也就是你保留的向量的大小。
cues.en: And if you can expand the latent vector back out and somehow this is far more efficient because you’re reducing… For example, maybe you’re reducing vec 32 or something like the size of the vector that you’re keeping.

cues.zh: 是的，拥有单独的一组键、值和查询，让它们两两匹配，而不是在交互中把它们全部压缩成一个，这或许有一些丰富性。
cues.en: Yeah, there’s perhaps some richness in having a separate set of keys and values and query that kind of pairwise match up versus compressing that all into one in that interaction at least.

cues.zh: 好的，而所有这些都是在处理内存受限的问题。
cues.en: Okay, and all of that is dealing with being memory bound.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，最终这如何映射到用户体验？
cues.en: I mean, ultimately, how does that map to the user experience?

cues.zh: 试图让那个——
cues.en: Trying to get the-

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 它映射到的两件事是：你现在可以把缓存做得大得多，因为你分配给 KV 缓存的空间更少了。
cues.en: The two things that it maps to is you can now make your cache a lot larger because you’ve less space allocated for the KV cache.

cues.zh: 你也许可以在更多东西上更激进地缓存，从而获得更多缓存命中，这有助于减少首 token 时间，原因就是前面描述的那些。
cues.en: You can maybe cache a lot more aggressively in a lot more things, so you get more cache hits, which are helpful for reducing the time to first token for the reasons that were kind of described earlier.

cues.zh: 然后第二点是，当你开始做推理，请求越来越多、批次越来越大时，生成 token 的速度基本不会明显变慢。
cues.en: And then the second being, when you start doing inference with more and more requests and larger and larger batch sizes, you don’t see much of a slowdown as it’s generating the tokens at the speed of that.

cues.zh: 嗯，这也能让你在某些情况下把 prompt 做得更大——
cues.en: Well, it also allows you to make your prompt bigger for certain-

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 对，所以 KV cache 的大小，等于所有 prompt 的大小乘以并行处理的 prompt 数量。
cues.en: Yeah, so the size of your KV cache is both the size of all your prompts multiplied by the number of prompts being processed in parallel.

cues.zh: 所以你可以增大这两个维度中的任意一个，对吧？
cues.en: So you could increase either those dimensions, right?

cues.zh: 也就是批次大小或 prompt 的大小，而不会降低生成 token 的延迟。
cues.en: The batch size or the size of your prompts without degrading the latency of generating tokens.

cues.zh: Arvid，你写了一篇博客文章《Shadow Workspace：在后台迭代代码》。
cues.en: Arvid, you wrote a blog post Shadow Workspace: Iterating on Code in the Background.

cues.zh: 那具体是怎么回事呢？
cues.en: So what’s going on [inaudible 01:04:59]?

cues.zh: 先说清楚，我们希望后台能发生很多事情，我们也在尝试很多东西。
cues.en: So to be clear, we want there to be a lot of stuff happening in the background, and we’re experimenting with a lot of things.

cues.zh: 目前，除了缓存预热或确定进入命令键提示的正确上下文之外，我们并没有太多其他事情发生。
cues.en: Right now, we don’t have much stuff happening other than the cache warming or figuring out the right context that goes into your command key prompts for example.

cues.zh: 但思路是，如果你能在后台消耗计算资源，那么你或许能在比仅仅预测接下来几行代码稍长的时间范围内帮助用户。
cues.en: But the idea is if you can actually spend computation in the background, then you can help the user maybe at a slightly longer time horizon than just predicting the next few lines that you’re going to make.

cues.zh: 但实际上，在接下来的10分钟里，你打算做什么？
cues.en: But actually in the next 10 minutes, what are you going to make?

cues.zh: 通过在后台进行，你可以投入更多计算资源来做这件事。
cues.en: And by doing it in background, you can spend more computation doing that.

cues.zh: 因此，我们实现的Shadow Workspace（我们内部用它来做实验）的思路是，要真正利用在后台做事的优势，你需要某种反馈信号返回给模型，因为否则的话，仅仅让模型思考更长时间就能获得更高的性能，o1就是一个很好的例子。
cues.en: And so the idea of the Shadow Workspace that we implemented, and we use it internally for experiments is that to actually get advantage of doing stuff in the background, you want some kind of feedback signal to give back to the model because otherwise you can get higher performance by just letting the model think for longer, and so o1 is a good example of that.

cues.zh: 但另一种提升性能的方法是让模型反复迭代并获取反馈。
cues.en: But another way you can improve performance is by letting the model iterate and get feedback.

cues.zh: 对程序员来说，一个非常重要的反馈来源就是语言服务器，也就是这个东西，大多数语言都有，而且每种语言都有各自独立的语言服务器。
cues.en: And so one very important piece of feedback when you’re a programmer is the language server, which is this thing, it exists for most different languages, and there’s a separate language server per language.

cues.zh: 它能告诉你：“你这里用错了类型”，然后给你报错，或者让你跳转到定义，某种程度上它理解你代码的结构。
cues.en: And it can tell you, “You’re using the wrong type here,” and then gives you an error, or it can allow you to go to definition and sort of understands the structure of your code.

cues.zh: 所以语言服务器是由……TypeScript 语言服务器由 TypeScript 团队开发，Rust 语言服务器由 Rust 团队开发，然后它们都通过语言服务器协议对接 VS Code。
cues.en: So language servers are extensions developed by… There is a TypeScript language server developed by the TypeScript people, a Rust language server developed by the Rust people, and then they all interface over the language server protocol to VS Code.

cues.zh: 这样 VS Code 就不需要把所有不同的语言都内置进去，而是可以直接复用现有的编译器基础设施。
cues.en: So that VS Code doesn’t need to have all of the different languages built into VS Code but rather you can use the existing compiler infrastructure.

cues.zh: 为了做 lint 检查，是做什么——
cues.en: For linting purposes, what-

cues.zh: 是用来做 lint 的。
cues.en: It’s for linting.

cues.zh: 用来跳转到定义，以及查看你正在使用的正确类型。
cues.en: It’s for going to definition and for seeing the right types that you’re using.

cues.zh: 所以它也在做类型检查。
cues.en: So it’s doing type checking also.

cues.zh: 是的，类型检查和跳转到引用。
cues.en: Yes, type checking and going to references.

cues.zh: 当你在一个大项目里工作时，你确实需要这个。
cues.en: And that’s like when you’re working in a big project, you kind of need that.

cues.zh: 如果没有这个，在大项目里写代码真的很难。
cues.en: If you don’t have that, it’s really hard to code in a big project.

cues.zh: 你能再说一遍，语言服务器协议通信这个东西在 Cursor 内部是怎么用的吗？
cues.en: Can you say, again, how that’s being used inside Cursor, the language server protocol communication thing?

cues.zh: 它在 Cursor 里的用法和 VS Code 一样，是展示给程序员的，但接下来的想法是，你想把同样的信息展示给模型，也就是 IM 模型，而且你想在不影响用户的情况下做到这一点，因为你想在后台做这件事。
cues.en: So it’s being used in Cursor to show to the programmer just like in VS Code, but then the idea is you want to show that same information to the models, the IM models, and you want to do that in a way that doesn’t affect the user because you want to do it in background.

cues.zh: 所以 Shadow Workspace 背后的想法是，好吧，我们能做的一种方式是启动一个隐藏的 Cursor 窗口，你可以设置这个标志，让它隐藏起来。
cues.en: And so the idea behind the Shadow Workspace was, okay, one way we can do this is we spawn a separate window of Cursor that’s hidden, and so you can set this flag in it and like turn it’s hidden.

cues.zh: 有一个窗口，但你实际上看不到它。
cues.en: There is a window but you don’t actually see it.

cues.zh: 在这个窗口里，AI 代理可以随意修改代码，只要不保存就行，因为它还是同一个文件夹，然后可以从 linter 获取反馈，跳转到定义，并迭代它们的代码。
cues.en: And inside of this window, the AI agents can modify code however they want as long as they don’t save it because it’s still the same folder and then can get feedback from the linters and go to definition and iterate on their code.

cues.zh: 所以实际上就是在后台运行一切，就好像……对，甚至可能运行代码。
cues.en: So literally run everything in the background as if… Right, maybe even run the code.

cues.zh: 所以那就是最终的版本，也是你想要的效果。
cues.en: So that’s the eventual version and that’s what you want.

cues.zh: 而那篇博客文章很大一部分实际上是在讲如何实现这一点，因为这有点棘手。
cues.en: And a lot of the blog post is actually about how do you make that happen because it’s a little bit tricky.

cues.zh: 你希望它运行在用户机器上，从而精确复现用户的环境。
cues.en: You want it to be on the user’s machine so that it exactly mirrors the user’s environment.

cues.zh: 然后在 Linux 上，你可以做一件很酷的事：真正镜像文件系统，让 AI 修改文件，它以为自己是在文件层面操作，但实际上这些改动存在内存里，你可以做一个类似内核的扩展来让它工作。
cues.en: And then on Linux, you can do this cool thing where you can actually mirror the file system and have the AI make changes to the files, and it thinks that it’s operating on the file level, but actually, that’s stored in memory and you can create this kernel-like extension to make it work.

cues.zh: 而在 Mac 和 Windows 上就稍微难一些，不过这是个有趣的技术问题，所以才这么做。
cues.en: Whereas on Mac and Windows, it’s a little bit more difficult, but it’s a fun technical problem, so that’s why.

cues.zh: 我挺喜欢的一个点子可能有点取巧，但很有意思：在保存时持有锁。
cues.en: One may be hacky but interesting idea that I like is holding a lock on saving.

cues.zh: 于是基本上，你可以让语言模型在保存到磁盘时持有锁，然后你操作的不再是磁盘上已保存的基准版本文件，而是之前的影子工作区，以及那些只存在于内存中的未保存内容——你仍然会看到 linter 报错，也可以继续写代码。
cues.en: And so basically, you can then have the language model kind of hold the lock on saving to disk and then instead of you operating in the ground truth version of the files that are saved to disk, you actually are operating what was the Shadow Workspace before and these unsaved things that only exist in memory that you still get linter errors for, and you can code in.

cues.zh: 然后当你尝试运行代码时，会看到一个小警告提示存在锁，如果你要并发操作，就会从语言服务器或 Shadow Workspace 那里把锁收回来。
cues.en: And then when you try to maybe run code, it’s just like there’s a small warning that there’s a lock, and then you kind of will take back the lock from the language server if you’re trying to do things concurrently or from the Shadow Workspace if you’re trying to do things concurrently.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，那样的未来真令人兴奋。
cues.en: That’s such an exciting future by the way.

cues.zh: 这有点跑题了，但让模型去修改文件，对人们来说挺吓人的，不过真的很酷——你只需让智能体执行一系列任务，第二天回来观察结果，就像对待一位同事那样。
cues.en: It’s a bit of a tangent, but to allow a model to change files, it’s scary for people but it’s really cool, to be able to just let the agent do a set of tasks and you come back the next day and kind of observe like it’s a colleague or something like that.

cues.zh: 我认为可能会有不同版本的运行能力，对于那些简单的事情，比如在用户编程时代表他们在几分钟内完成的操作，让它在用户本地机器上运行是合理的。
cues.en: And I think there may be different versions of runability where, for the simple things where you’re doing things in the span of a few minutes on behalf of the user as they’re programming, it makes sense to make something work locally in their machine.

cues.zh: 我觉得，对于那些更激进、改动更大、耗时更长的操作，你大概会想在某种沙箱远程环境里做，而这就引出了另一个极其棘手的问题：你怎么才能精确复现，或者说大部分复现到实际上等效的程度，在远程沙箱里运行用户环境的代码。
cues.en: I think for the more aggressive things where you’re making larger changes that take longer periods of time, you’ll probably want to do this in some sandbox remote environment and that’s another incredibly tricky problem of how do you exactly reproduce or mostly reproduce to the point of it being effectively equivalent for running code the user’s environment with this remote sandbox.

cues.zh: 我很好奇你想要什么样的编码智能体？
cues.en: I’m curious what kind of agents you want for coding?

cues.zh: 你想让它们找 bug 吗？
cues.en: Do you want them to find bugs?

cues.zh: 你想让它们实现新功能吗？
cues.en: Do you want them to implement new features?

cues.zh: 你想要什么样的智能体？
cues.en: What agents do you want?

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我想到智能体的时候，并不只想到编码。
cues.en: So by the way, when I think about agents, I don’t think just about coding.

cues.zh: 我觉得就这期播客而言，还有视频剪辑以及很多……如果你看看 Adobe，很多……背后都有代码。
cues.en: I think so for this particular podcast, there’s video editing and a lot of… If you look in Adobe, a lot… There’s code behind.

cues.zh: 这代码文档写得很差，但你可以用代码和 Premiere 交互，基本上所有上传、我在 YouTube 上做的一切，你大概也能想到，我全都是通过代码完成的，包括翻译和配音，所有这些。
cues.en: It’s very poorly documented code, but you can interact with Premiere, for example, using code, and basically all the uploading, everything I do on YouTube, everything as you could probably imagine, I do all of that through code and including translation and overdubbing, all of this.

cues.zh: 所以我设想了所有这些类型的任务。
cues.en: So I envision all of those kinds of tasks.

cues.zh: 把很多不直接涉及剪辑的任务自动化，这样。
cues.en: So automating many of the tasks that don’t have to do directly with the editing, so that.

cues.zh: 好，这就是我当时在想的。
cues.en: Okay, that’s what I was thinking about.

cues.zh: 但就编程而言，我基本上会考虑找 bug，很多层面的找 bug，还有像逻辑 bug 这样的找 bug，不是逻辑那种玄学 bug 之类的。
cues.en: But in terms of coding, I would be fundamentally thinking about bug finding, many levels of kind of bug finding and also bug finding like logical bugs, not logical like spiritual bugs or something.

cues.zh: 比如实现的大方向，那种东西。
cues.en: Ones like big directions of implementation, that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 神奇的[听不清 01:11:39]和缺陷发现。
cues.en: Magical [inaudible 01:11:39] and bug finding.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，这些模型在直接提示找缺陷时表现这么差，真的很有意思。
cues.en: I mean, it’s really interesting that these models are so bad at bug finding when just naively prompted to find a bug.

cues.zh: 它们的校准非常糟糕。
cues.en: They’re incredibly poorly calibrated.

cues.zh: 即使是最聪明的模型。
cues.en: Even the smartest models.

cues.zh: 没错，即使是 o1。
cues.en: Exactly, even o1.

cues.zh: 你怎么解释这个？
cues.en: How do you explain that?

cues.zh: 有什么好的直觉吗？
cues.en: Is there a good intuition?

cues.zh: 我认为这些模型确实是预训练分布的强烈反映，我确实认为随着损失越来越低，它们会泛化，但我不认为损失和规模已经足够……损失足够低，以至于它们能在代码上真正完全泛化。
cues.en: I think these models are really strong reflection of the pre-training distribution, and I do think they generalize as the loss gets lower and lower, but I don’t think the loss and the scale is quite… The loss is low enough such that they’re really fully generalizing on code.

cues.zh: 我们使用这些东西的目的，前沿模型非常擅长的事情，实际上是代码生成和问答。
cues.en: The things that we use these things for, the frontier models that they’re quite good at, are really code generation and question answering.

cues.zh: 而这些内容在预训练中大量存在，GitHub 上的所有代码，规模达到数万亿个 token，还有 Stack Overflow 上的问答，也许还有 GitHub issues。
cues.en: And these things exist in massive quantities in pre-training with all of the code in GitHub on the scale of many, many trillions of tokens and questions and answers on things like stack overflow and maybe GitHub issues.

cues.zh: 所以当你试图推动这些在网上几乎不存在的东西时，比如 Cursor Tab 的目标——根据目前所做的编辑预测下一次编辑——脆弱性就显现出来了。
cues.en: And so when you try to push one of these things that really don’t exist very much online, like for example, the Cursor Tab objective of predicting the next edit given the edits done so far, the brittleness kind of shows.

cues.zh: 然后 bug 检测是另一个很好的例子，实际上真正检测真实 bug 并提出修复的样本并不多，模型在这方面确实很吃力。
cues.en: And then bug detection is another great example, where there aren’t really that many examples of actually detecting real bugs and then proposing fixes and the models just kind of really struggle at it.

cues.zh: 但我认为这是一个迁移模型的问题，就像你从一般代码上的预训练模型获得极好的迁移到 Cursor Tab 目标一样。
cues.en: But I think it’s a question of transferring the model in the same way that you get this fantastic transfer from pre-trained models just on code in general to the Cursor Tab objective.

cues.zh: 在擅长代码到缺陷检测的通用模型上，你会看到非常非常相似的情况。
cues.en: You’ll see a very, very similar thing with generalized models that are really good at code to bug detection.

cues.zh: 只需要朝那个方向轻轻推一把就行。
cues.en: It just takes a little bit of kind nudging in that direction.

cues.zh: 要说清楚，我觉得它们对代码的理解相当不错。
cues.en: Look to be clear, I think they sort of understand code really well.

cues.zh: 在预训练过程中，所构建的表征几乎可以肯定，在数据流的某个地方，模型知道也许有些可疑的东西在发生。
cues.en: While they’re being pre-trained, the representation that’s being built up almost certainly like somewhere in the stream, the model knows that maybe there’s something sketchy going on.

cues.zh: 它多少有点可疑，但真正要把这种可疑性引出来……部分原因是，人类对于哪些缺陷真正重要有着很好的校准。
cues.en: It sort of has some sketchiness but actually eliciting the sketchiness to actually… Part of it is that humans are really calibrated on which bugs are really important.

cues.zh: 这不仅仅是说“有些可疑”。
cues.en: It’s not just actually saying there’s something sketchy.

cues.zh: 而是说，这个可疑是无关紧要的，还是那种会让服务器宕机的可疑。
cues.en: It’s like it’s this sketchy trivial, it’s this sketchy like you’re going to take the server down.

cues.zh: 其中一部分可能是文化知识，比如为什么资深工程师很厉害，因为他们知道三年前有人写了一段非常可疑的代码，导致服务器宕机，而你可能只是……这东西是个实验。
cues.en: Part of it is maybe the cultural knowledge of why is a staff engineer is good because they know that three years ago someone wrote a really sketchy piece of code that took the server down and as opposed to maybe you just… This thing is an experiment.

cues.zh: 所以有些 bug 没关系，你只是在做实验，找找感觉。
cues.en: So a few bugs are fine, you’re just trying to experiment and get the feel of the thing.

cues.zh: 所以如果你在写实验时模型变得很烦人，那很糟糕，但如果你在写超级生产级的东西，比如在写数据库。
cues.en: And so if the model gets really annoying when you’re writing an experiment, that’s really bad, but if you’re writing something for super production, you’re writing a database.

cues.zh: 你在写 Postgres 或 Linux 之类的代码。
cues.en: You’re writing code in Postgres or Linux or whatever.

cues.zh: 你就是 Linus Torvalds。
cues.en: You’re Linus Torvalds.

cues.zh: 哪怕只是一个边缘情况也是不可接受的，还要有对用户有多偏执的校准，就像——
cues.en: It’s sort of unacceptable to have even an edge case and just having the calibration of how paranoid is the user and like-

cues.zh: 但即便如此，如果你把偏执拉满，它还是不太能完全理解。
cues.en: But even then if you’re putting in a maximum paranoia, it still just doesn’t quite get it.

cues.zh: 是啊，是啊。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我是说，但这对人类来说也很难理解哪行代码重要，哪行不重要。
cues.en: I mean, but this is hard for humans too to understand which line of code is important, which is not.

cues.zh: 我觉得你网站上有一条原则说，如果一段代码可能造成很大破坏，就应该加一条注释写着：“这行代码很危险。”
cues.en: I think one of your principles on a website says if a code can do a lot of damage, one should add a comment that say, “This line of code is dangerous.”

cues.zh: 而且全大写，重复10遍。
cues.en: And all caps, repeated 10 times.

cues.zh: 不，你说的是函数里每一行代码都得……这挺深刻的，这说明了人类的某些特点，因为工程师会往前走，甚至同一个人也可能忘记一个函数怎么能弄沉泰坦尼克号。
cues.en: No, you say for every single line of code inside the function you have to… And that’s quite profound, that says something about human beings because the engineers move on, even the same person might just forget how it can sink the Titanic a single function.

cues.zh: 光看那一小段代码，你可能没法那么清楚地直觉到这一点。
cues.en: You might not intuit that quite clearly by looking at the single piece of code.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得这一点也部分适用于今天的AI模型，如果你真的在每一行都写上危险、危险、危险，模型会更关注这些地方，也更可能在那个区域发现bug。
cues.en: And I think that one is partially also for today’s AI models where if you actually write dangerous, dangerous, dangerous in every single line, the models will pay more attention to that and will be more likely to find bugs in that region.

cues.zh: 其实直接给代码标注它能造成多大破坏，就是个非常好的做法。
cues.en: That’s actually just straight up a really good practice of labeling code of how much damages can do.

cues.zh: 是啊。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我是说，这有争议。
cues.en: I mean, it’s controversial.

cues.zh: 有些人觉得它很丑。
cues.en: Some people think it’s ugly.

cues.zh: Sualeh 就不喜欢它。
cues.en: Sualeh does not like it.

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得……其实，这实际上是我从 Arvid 那里学到的东西之一，从审美上我不喜欢它，但我认为它确实有用，因为模型和人类都会忘掉很多东西，而且很容易犯个小错就导致……直接把服务器搞崩。
cues.en: Well, I think it’s… In fact, I actually think this is one of the things I learned from Arvid is sort of aesthetically I don’t like it, but I think there’s certainly something where it’s useful for the models and humans just forget a lot, and it’s really easy to make a small mistake and cause… Just bring down the server.

cues.zh: 当然，我们会做大量测试之类的，但总有些事你必须非常小心。
cues.en: Of course, we test a lot and whatever, but there’s always these things that you have to be very careful.

cues.zh: 是啊，就像普通的文档字符串，我觉得人们改代码时经常只是扫一眼，心想“哦，我知道怎么做”，你真的需要向他们指出来，这样才不会漏掉。
cues.en: Yeah, like with just normal docstrings, I think people will often just skim it when making a change and think, “Oh, I know how to do this,” and you really need to point it out to them so that doesn’t slip through.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 得提醒你，你可能造成很大破坏，这点我们平时不太会去想。
cues.en: You have to be reminded that you could do a lot of damage that’s like we don’t really think about that.

cues.zh: 你会想：“好，我怎么搞懂它怎么运作，好去改进它？”你不会去想另一个方向，就是它可能——
cues.en: You think about, “Okay, how do I figure out how this works so I can improve it?” You don’t think about the other direction that it could-

cues.zh: 直到我们对一切都有了形式化验证，那时你想怎么做都行，只要证明通过，你就能确定自己没引入 bug。
cues.en: Until we have formal verification for everything, then you can do whatever you want and you know for certain that you have not introduced a bug if the proof pass.

cues.zh: 具体来说，你觉得那个未来会是什么样？
cues.en: Well, concretely, what do you think that future would look like?

cues.zh: 我觉得人们干脆就不再写测试了，模型会建议……你写一个函数，模型会建议一份规约，你来审这份规约。
cues.en: I think people will just not write to tests anymore, and the model will suggest… You write a function, the model will suggest a spec, and you review the spec.

cues.zh: 同时，聪明的推理模型会计算出一个证明，说明实现符合规约，我觉得大多数函数都会这样。
cues.en: And in the meantime, smart reasoning model computes a proof that the implementation follows the spec, and I think that happens for most functions.

cues.zh: 你觉得这是不是多少触及了你之前谈到的那个难点——用软件明确表达你想要什么意图，有时候可能是因为意图本身就很难明确，那么要证明它确实符合你的意图也会非常困难？
cues.en: Do you think this gets at a little bit some of the stuff you were talking about earlier with the difficulty of specifying intent for what you want with software, where sometimes it might be because the intent is really hard to specify, it’s also then going to be really hard to prove that it’s actually matching whatever your intent is?

cues.zh: 你觉得规格很难生成？
cues.en: You think that spec is hard to generate?

cues.zh: 是的，或者对于给定的规格，也许你可以……我觉得有个问题是，你真的能做形式化验证吗？
cues.en: Yeah, or just for a given spec, maybe you can… I think there is a question of, can you actually do the formal verification?

cues.zh: 那可能吗？
cues.en: Is that possible?

cues.zh: 我觉得那里还有更多可以深挖的，但另外还有——
cues.en: I think that there’s more to dig into there, but then also-

cues.zh: 即使你有规格？
cues.en: Even if you have the spec?

cues.zh: 如果你有规格——
cues.en: If you have the spec-

cues.zh: 即使你有规格，规格是用自然语言写的吗？
cues.en: Even if you have the spec, is the spec written in natural language?

cues.zh: 还是说——
cues.en: Or is it-

cues.zh: 不，[听不清 01:18:21] 规格会是形式化的。
cues.en: No, [inaudible 01:18:21] the spec would be formal.

cues.zh: 但那会有多简单呢[听不清 01:18:26]？
cues.en: But how easier would that be [inaudible 01:18:26]?

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那么我觉得，你关心的是那些在规范语言里不容易被很好地描述的东西。
cues.en: So then I think that you care about things that are not going to be easily well specified in the spec language.

cues.zh: 我明白了，我明白了。
cues.en: I see, I see.

cues.zh: 这或许可以成为反对形式化验证的一个论据，就是说你只需要这个。
cues.en: Would be maybe an argument against formal verification is all you need.

cues.zh: 令人担忧的是，有这么一份庞大的文档——
cues.en: The worry is there’s this massive document-

cues.zh: [听不清 01:18:39]取代单元测试之类的东西，当然。
cues.en: [inaudible 01:18:39] replacing something like unit tests, sure.

cues.zh: 是的，是的。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得你或许也可以演进规范语言，来捕捉一些它们目前还无法真正捕捉的东西。
cues.en: I think you can probably also evolve the spec languages to capture some of the things that they don’t really capture right now.

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I don’t know.

cues.zh: 我觉得这非常令人兴奋。
cues.en: I think it’s very exciting.

cues.zh: 而且你说的不只是单个函数，你说的是整个代码库。
cues.en: And you’re speaking not just about single functions, you’re speaking about entire code bases.

cues.zh: 我觉得整个代码库更难，但那正是我很想拥有的，而且我认为这应该是可能的。
cues.en: I think entire code bases is harder, but that is what I would love to have and I think it should be possible.

cues.zh: 而且因为你甚至可以……最近有很多工作，可以形式化验证一直到硬件层面，所以通过……你先形式化验证 C 代码，然后通过 GCC 编译器形式化验证，再通过 Verilog 一直到硬件。
cues.en: And because you can even… There’s a lot of work recently where you can prove formally verified down to the hardware, so through the… You formally verify the C code and then you formally verify through the GCC compiler and then through the Verilog down to the hardware.

cues.zh: 那是个极其庞大的系统，但它确实能跑通。
cues.en: And that’s incredibly big system, but it actually works.

cues.zh: 我觉得大型代码库也类似，它们就像多层系统。
cues.en: And I think big code bases are sort of similar in that and they’re like multi-layered system.

cues.zh: 如果你能把它分解，并对每个部分做形式化验证，那我认为这应该是可行的。
cues.en: And if you can decompose it and formally verify each part, then I think it should be possible.

cues.zh: 我觉得规格说明这个问题是个真问题，但是……
cues.en: I think this specification problem is a real problem, but…

cues.zh: 你如何处理副作用，或者你如何处理，我猜是外部依赖，比如调用 Stripe API？
cues.en: How do you handle side effects or how do you handle, I guess, external dependencies like calling the Stripe API?

cues.zh: 也许 Stripe 会为他们的 API 写一份规格说明。
cues.en: Maybe Stripe would write a spec for their API.

cues.zh: 但你不能对所有事情都这么做。
cues.en: But you can’t do this for everything.

cues.zh: 你能对你用到的所有东西都这么做吗？
cues.en: Can you do this for everything you use?

cues.zh: 你怎么对……如果有一种语言……也许人们会把语言模型当作所写程序中的原语，并且对它存在依赖，那你现在怎么把这一点纳入进来？
cues.en: How do you do it for… If there’s a language… Maybe people will use language models as primitives in the programs they write, and there’s a dependence on it and how do you now include that?

cues.zh: 我觉得你也许仍然能证明这一点。
cues.en: I think you might be able to prove that still.

cues.zh: 证明语言模型的什么？
cues.en: Prove what about language models?

cues.zh: 我觉得有可能真的可以证明一个语言模型是对齐的，比如，或者你可以证明它确实给出正确答案。
cues.en: I think it feels possible that you could actually prove that a language model is aligned for example, or you can prove that it actually gives the right answer.

cues.zh: 那就是梦想。
cues.en: That’s the dream.

cues.zh: 是啊，那就是……我是说，如果可能的话。
cues.en: Yeah, that is… I mean, if it’s possible.

cues.zh: 这就是你的“我有一个梦想”演讲。
cues.en: That’s your I have a dream speech.

cues.zh: 如果可能的话，那肯定有助于确保你的代码没有 bug，并确保 AI 不会毁灭全人类文明。
cues.en: If it’s possible, that will certainly help with making sure your code doesn’t have bugs and making sure AI doesn’t destroy all human civilization.

cues.zh: 从AI安全的整个范畴一直到查找bug。
cues.en: So the full spectrum of AI safety to just bug finding.

cues.zh: 你说模型在查找bug方面很吃力。
cues.en: So you said the models struggle with bug finding.

cues.zh: 希望在哪里？
cues.en: What’s the hope?

cues.zh: 我最初的希望是——Michael也可以补充——它应该先帮忙抓那些低级bug。
cues.en: My hope initially is, and I can let Michael chime in too, but it was like it should first help with the stupid bugs.

cues.zh: 它应该快速查询，抓住那些低级bug，比如差一错误……有时候你在注释里写了一种做法，实际却做了另一种。
cues.en: It should query quickly, catch the stupid bugs off by one error is like… Sometimes you write something in a comment and do the other way.

cues.zh: 这很常见。
cues.en: It’s very common.

cues.zh: 我也这样。
cues.en: I do this.

cues.zh: 我在注释里写小于，实际可能写成大于之类的。
cues.en: I write less than in a comment and I maybe write the greater than or something like that.

cues.zh: 然后模型就说：“嗯，你看起来有点可疑。
cues.en: And the model is like, “Yeah, you looks sketchy.

cues.zh: 你确定要这么做吗？”但最终，它也应该能抓住更难的bug。
cues.en: You sure you want to do that?” But eventually, it should be able to catch harder bugs too.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得还有一点很重要：拥有好的bug查找模型，感觉是让AI为你做越来越多编程的必要条件——如果AI在为你构建越来越多的系统，你不仅需要生成，还需要验证。
cues.en: And I think that it’s also important to note that this is… Having good bug, finding models feels necessary to get to the highest reaches of having AI do more and more programming for you, where you’re going to… If AI is building more and more of the system for you, you need to not just generate but also verify.

cues.zh: 而如果没有这一点，我们之前谈到的编程中与这些模型相关的一些问题就会变得难以为继。
cues.en: And without that, some of the problems that we’ve talked about before with programming, with these models will just become untenable.

cues.zh: 所以这不仅仅是为了人类，比如你写了个 bug，我写了个 bug，帮我找出这个 bug，而且还要能够验证 AI 的代码并检查它，这非常重要。
cues.en: So it’s not just for humans like you write a bug, I write a bug, find the bug for me, but it’s also being able to verify the AI’s code and check it is really important.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 那么你究竟如何做到这一点呢？
cues.en: And then how do you actually do this?

cues.zh: 我们在晚餐讨论中有过很多争论，关于究竟如何训练一个 bug 模型，但一个非常流行的想法是，引入一个 bug 可能比实际找到这个 bug 更容易。
cues.en: We have had a lot of contentious dinner discussions of how do you actually train a bug model, but one very popular idea is it’s kind of potentially easy to introduce a bug than actually finding the bug.

cues.zh: 因此，你可以训练一个模型在现有代码中引入 bug，然后你可以训练一个反向 bug 模型，它可以使用这些合成数据来发现 bug。
cues.en: And so you can train a model to introduce bugs in existing code and then you can train a reverse bug model then that can find bugs using this synthetic data.

cues.zh: 这是一个例子，但关于如何做到这一点还有很多想法 [听不清 01:22:22]。
cues.en: So that’s one example, but there are lots of ideas for how to [inaudible 01:22:22].

cues.zh: 你也可以做很多工作，甚至不局限于模型层面，比如拿最大的模型，然后也许让它们访问大量不仅仅是代码的信息。
cues.en: You can also do a bunch of work not even at the model level of taking the biggest models and then maybe giving them access to a lot of information that’s not just the code.

cues.zh: 盯着一个文件想“bug 在哪儿？”是个挺难的问题。这对人类来说往往也很难，对吧？
cues.en: It’s kind of a hard problem to stare at a file and be like, “Where’s the bug?” And that’s hard for humans often, right?

cues.zh: 所以很多时候你得运行代码，能查看追踪信息、用调试器单步执行，这是另一个完全不同的方向，趋势也倾向于那边。
cues.en: And so often you have to run the code and being able to see things like traces and step through a debugger, there’s another whole other direction where it tends toward that.

cues.zh: 也可能这里有两种不同的产品形态。
cues.en: It could also be that there are two different product form factors here.

cues.zh: 可能是你有一个非常专用的模型，速度很快，在后台运行，试图找出 bug。
cues.en: It could be that you have a really specialty model that’s quite fast that’s running in the background and trying to spot bugs.

cues.zh: 有时候，就像Arvid之前举的那个例子，可能是个恶意输入框的bug。
cues.en: And it might be that sometimes sort of to Arvid’s earlier example about some nefarious input box bug.

cues.zh: 有时候你可能想……你知道有个bug，你不是在随便验证假设，而是觉得“这是个问题，我真的很想解决它”，然后你投入海量的算力去攻克它，甚至愿意花50美元或更多来解决那个bug。
cues.en: It might be that sometimes you want to like… You know there’s a bug, you’re not just checking hypothesis free, you’re like, “This is a problem, I really want to solve it,” and you zap that with tons and tons and tons of compute, and you’re willing to put in $50 to solve that bug or something even more.

cues.zh: 你有没有想过把金钱整合进这整套东西里？
cues.en: Have you thought about integrating money into this whole thing?

cues.zh: 如果你找到了一个bug，甚至生成了我真的很欣赏的代码，我大概会付一大笔钱。
cues.en: I would pay probably a large amount of money if you found a bug or even generated code that I really appreciated.

cues.zh: 几天前我开始用Cursor的时候有个瞬间，它完美生成了三个函数，用来跟YouTube API交互，更新字幕以适配不同语言的本地化。
cues.en: I had a moment a few days ago when I started using Cursor where it generated perfect three functions for interacting with the YouTube API to update captions for localization in different languages.

cues.zh: API 文档写得不太好，代码也是……我 Google 了好一阵子。
cues.en: The API documentation is not very good and the code across, if I… I googled it for a while.

cues.zh: 我找不到确切的答案，信息又多又乱，而 Cursor 生成得完美无缺。
cues.en: I couldn’t find exactly, there’s a lot of confusing information, and Cursor generated perfectly.

cues.zh: 我就往后一靠，读代码，心想：“这是对的。
cues.en: I just sit back, I read the code, I was like, “This is correct.

cues.zh: 我测试过了，没问题。”我就想：“我想给小费。”我想要一个按钮写着“给你 5 美元”。就为了支持这家公司、支持这个界面，做得这么好值得打赏。
cues.en: I tested it, it’s correct.” I was like, “I want to tip.” I want a button that goes, “Here’s $5.” One that’s really good just to support the company and support what the interface is.

cues.zh: 另一个是，这大概能发出一个强烈的信号，就像“干得好”。
cues.en: And the other is that probably sends a strong signal like good job.

cues.zh: 所以这比单纯接受代码要强得多的信号。
cues.en: So there’s this much stronger signal than just accepting the code.

cues.zh: 你实际上是在明确地表达“干得好”。
cues.en: You just actually send a strong good job.

cues.zh: 还有找 bug 这块，显然有很多人愿意为 bug 赏金花大价钱，对吧？
cues.en: That and for bug finding, obviously, there’s a lot of people that would pay a huge amount of money for a bug bounty thing, right?

cues.zh: 你们想过这个吗？
cues.en: You guys think about that?

cues.zh: 想过，这在公司内部是个有争议的想法。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s a controversial idea inside the company.

cues.zh: 我觉得这某种程度上取决于你有多相信人性。
cues.en: I think it sort of depends on how much you believe in humanity almost.

cues.zh: 我觉得如果你不花钱就能试着找 bug，那会很酷。
cues.en: I think it would be really cool if you spend nothing to try to find a bug.

cues.zh: 如果没找到 bug，你就花 0 美元。
cues.en: And if it doesn’t find a bug, you spend $0.

cues.zh: 如果找到了 bug，你点击接受，它还会在括号里显示比如 1 美元。
cues.en: And then if it does find a bug and you click accept, then it also shows in parentheses like $1.

cues.zh: 所以你花 1 美元来接受这个 bug。
cues.en: And so you spend $1 to accept the bug.

cues.zh: 但我觉得对于那个特定的系统，我们……所以具体细节上，我们做的显然是当……我们把你的所有代码分块，然后把代码发上去做嵌入，我们对代码进行嵌入。
cues.en: But I think for that particular system, we’ve… So for concrete details, the thing we do is obviously we upload when… We chunk up all of your code, and then we send up the code for embedding and we embed the code.

cues.zh: 然后我们把嵌入存储在数据库里，但实际上我们并不存储任何代码。
cues.en: And then we store the embeddings in a database, but we don’t actually store any of the code.

cues.zh: 然后还有一些原因，是为了确保我们不会引入客户端 bug，因为我们对客户端 bug 非常非常偏执。
cues.en: And then there’s reasons around making sure that we don’t introduce client bugs because we’re very, very paranoid about client bugs.

cues.zh: 我们把很多细节存储在服务器上。
cues.en: We store much of the details on the server.

cues.zh: 一切都是加密的。
cues.en: Everything is encrypted.

cues.zh: 所以技术挑战之一始终是确保本地索引、本地代码库状态与服务器上的状态一致。
cues.en: So one of the technical challenges is always making sure that the local index, the local code base state is the same as the state that is on the server.

cues.zh: 从技术上讲，我们最终采用的方法是，对每个文件保留一个哈希值，然后对每个文件夹也保留一个哈希值，这个哈希值是其所有子项哈希值的汇总。
cues.en: The way, technically, we ended up doing that is, for every single file you can keep this hash, and then for every folder you can keep a hash, which is the hash of all of its children.

cues.zh: 你可以递归地这样做，直到最顶层。
cues.en: You can recursively do that until the top.

cues.zh: 为什么要搞得那么复杂？
cues.en: Why do something complicated?

cues.zh: 一种做法是，你可以为每个文件保留一个哈希值，然后每分钟尝试下载服务器上的哈希值，找出服务器上不存在的文件。
cues.en: One thing you could do is you could keep a hash for every file and every minute, you could try to download the hashes that are on the server, figure out what are the files that don’t exist on the server.

cues.zh: 也许你刚创建了一个新文件，也许你刚删除了一个文件，也许你检出了一个新分支，然后尝试协调客户端和服务器之间的状态。
cues.en: Maybe you just created a new file, maybe you just deleted a file, maybe you checked out a new branch, and try to reconcile the state between the client and the server.

cues.zh: 但这会在客户端引入极其庞大的网络开销。
cues.en: But that introduces absolutely ginormous network overhead both on the client side.

cues.zh: 如果你用的是 Cursor，没人真希望我们一直狂刷他们的 WiFi。
cues.en: Nobody really wants us to hammer their WiFi all the time if you’re using Cursor.

cues.zh: 而且，这还会给数据库带来极其庞大的开销。
cues.en: But also, it would introduce ginormous overhead on the database.

cues.zh: 它每秒都要读取这几十 TB 的数据库，接近 20 TB 左右的数据。
cues.en: It would be reading these tens of terabytes database, approaching 20 terabytes or something data base every second.

cues.zh: 这简直太疯狂了。
cues.en: That’s just crazy.

cues.zh: 你肯定不想那么做。
cues.en: You definitely don’t want to do that.

cues.zh: 所以你要做的，就是只去核对项目根部的那个单一哈希。
cues.en: So what you do, you just try to reconcile the single hash, which is at the root of the project.

cues.zh: 然后如果发现不匹配，再去找出所有不一致的地方。
cues.en: And then if something mismatches, then you go, you find where all the things disagree.

cues.zh: 也许你会查看子节点，看看哈希是否匹配。
cues.en: Maybe you look at the children and see if the hashes match.

cues.zh: 如果哈希不匹配，就再去看它们的子节点，以此类推。
cues.en: If the hashes don’t match, go look at their children and so on.

cues.zh: 但你只在出现不匹配的情况下才这么做。
cues.en: But you only do that in the scenario where things don’t match.

cues.zh: 对大多数人来说，大多数时候，哈希值都是匹配的。
cues.en: For most people, most of the time, the hashes match.

cues.zh: 所以这就像一种分层协调——
cues.en: So it’s like a hierarchical reconciliation-

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: ……哈希值的——
cues.en: … of hashes-

cues.zh: 差不多是这样。
cues.en: Something like that.

cues.zh: 对，这叫默克尔树。
cues.en: Yeah, it’s called a Merkle tree.

cues.zh: 对，默克尔。
cues.en: Yeah, Merkle.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 是啊，看到你必须把这些问题都想透，挺酷的。
cues.en: Yeah, this is cool to see that you have to think through all these problems.

cues.zh: 它之所以变难，就是因为使用它的人越来越多，而且有些客户的代码库真的非常非常大，大到……我们最初重构的暗色代码库虽然大，但还比不上某些存在了20年、文件数量巨大的公司，而你还想把它扩展到众多程序员身上。
cues.en: The reason it’s gotten hard is just because the number of people using it and some of your customers have really, really large code bases to the point where… We originally reordered dark code base, which is big, but it’s just not the size of some company that’s been there for 20 years and has a ginormous number of files and you want to scale that across programmers.

cues.zh: 有所有这些细节，构建简单的东西很容易，但把它扩展到很多人、很多公司显然是个难题，而这实际上独立于……所以这就是这种扩展的一部分。
cues.en: There’s all these details where building the simple thing is easy, but scaling it to a lot of people, a lot of companies is obviously a difficult problem, which is independent of, actually… so that there’s part of this scaling.

cues.zh: 我们目前的解决方案也在不断涌现新想法，显然我们正在推进这些想法，然后在过去几周、几个月里把它们全面扩展。
cues.en: Our current solution is also coming up with new ideas that, obviously, we’re working on, but then scaling all of that in the last few weeks, months.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 这个索引系统里还有很多巧妙的东西、额外的设计。
cues.en: There are a lot of clever things, additional things that go into this indexing system.

cues.zh: 比如，成本上的瓶颈并不是在向量数据库或数据库里存储这些东西。
cues.en: For example, the bottleneck in terms of costs is not soaring things in the vector database or the database.

cues.zh: 真正的瓶颈其实是嵌入代码。
cues.en: It’s actually embedding the code.

cues.zh: 你不会想为公司里每个使用完全相同代码的人重新嵌入整个代码库——除非他们可能在不同分支上，有几个不同的文件，或者做了一些本地改动。
cues.en: You don’t want to re-embed the code base for every single person in a company that is using the same exact code except for maybe they’re a different branch with a few different files or they’ve made a few local changes.

cues.zh: 因为嵌入又是瓶颈，你可以用这个巧妙的技巧，就不必操心处理分支和其他数据库的复杂性，只需根据给定块的哈希计算出的向量做一些缓存。
cues.en: Because again, embeddings are the bottleneck, you can do this one clever trick and not have to worry about the complexity of dealing with branches and the other databases where you just have some cash on the actual vectors computed from the hash of a given chunk.

cues.zh: 这意味着，当公司里第 n 个人去嵌入他们的代码库时，速度真的非常快。
cues.en: So this means that when the nth person at a company goes and embed their code base, it’s really, really fast.

cues.zh: 你完成这一切，实际上完全不需要把任何代码存储在我们的服务器上。
cues.en: You do all this without actually storing any code on our servers at all.

cues.zh: 不存储任何代码数据。
cues.en: No code data is stored.

cues.zh: 我们只是把向量存进向量数据库和向量缓存里。
cues.en: We just store the vectors in the vector database and the vector cache.

cues.zh: 目前，从索引代码库中获得的最大收益是什么？
cues.en: What’s the biggest gains at this time you get from indexing the code base?

cues.zh: 纯粹出于好奇，用户能得到什么好处？
