cues.en: It seems like longer term, there’ll be more and more benefit, but in the short term, just asking questions of the code base, what’s the usefulness of that?

cues.zh: 我觉得最明显的一点就是，你想在庞大的代码库里找到某件事发生在哪里，而你只有模糊的记忆：“好吧，我想找到我们做 X 的那个地方”，但在普通文本搜索里你并不确切知道该搜什么。
cues.en: I think the most obvious one is just, you want to find out where something is happening in your large code base, and you have a fuzzy memory of, “Okay, I want to find the place where we do X,” but you don’t exactly know what to search for in a normal text search.

cues.zh: 所以你向聊天提问，敲下 command enter，带着代码库来提问。
cues.en: So you ask a chat, you hit command enter to ask with the code base chat.

cues.zh: 然后很多时候，它就能找到你心里想的那个正确位置。
cues.en: And then very often, it finds the right place that you were thinking of.

cues.zh: 就像你提到的，未来我觉得它只会越来越强大，我们正在大力提升检索的质量。
cues.en: Like you mentioned, in the future, I think there’s only going to get more and more powerful, where we’re working a lot on improving the quality of our retrieval.

cues.zh: 我觉得这方面的上限真的比人们以为的要高得多。
cues.en: I think the ceiling for that is really, really much higher than people give the credit for.

cues.zh: 这里有个值得问的问题，你有没有考虑过，为什么没怎么做本地化的东西，让你能实现……好像大家讨论起来都觉得特别难做。
cues.en: One question that’s good to ask here, have you considered and why haven’t you much done local stuff to where you can do the… It seems like everything was just discussed as exceptionally difficult to do.

cues.zh: 要上云，你就得考虑缓存和大型代码库这些事，大量程序员共用同一个代码库。
cues.en: To go to the cloud, you have to think about all these things with the caching and the large code base where a large number of programmers are using the same code base.

cues.zh: 你得弄清楚这个难题。
cues.en: You have to figure out the puzzle of that.

cues.zh: 很多软件的大部分重计算都是在本地完成的。
cues.en: A lot of it, most software just does this heavy computational stuff locally.

cues.zh: 那你考虑过在本地做嵌入吗？
cues.en: So have you considered doing embeddings locally?

cues.zh: 考虑过，我觉得在本地做会很酷。
cues.en: Yeah, we thought about it, and I think it would be cool to do it locally.

cues.zh: 但我觉得真的很难。
cues.en: I think it’s just really hard.

cues.zh: 有一点要记住，有些用户用的是最新的 MacBook Pro，但大多数用户，超过 80% 的用户用的是 Windows 机器，其中很多性能并不强。
cues.en: One thing to keep in mind is that some of our users use the latest MacBook Pro, but most of our users, more than 80% of our users are in Windows machines, which many of them are not very powerful.

cues.zh: 所以本地模型实际上只能在最新的电脑上运行，而且把它集成进来开销也很大。
cues.en: So local models really only works on the latest computers, and it’s also a big overhead to build that in.

cues.zh: 所以即使我们想做，目前也不是我们能重点推进的事。
cues.en: So even if we would like to do that, it’s currently not something that we are able to focus on.

cues.zh: 我知道有些人在这么做，我觉得很好，但尤其是随着模型越来越大，你想用更大的模型做更花哨的事，在本地做就更难了。
cues.en: I think there are some people that do that, and I think that’s great, but especially as models get bigger and bigger and you want to do fancier things with bigger models, it becomes even harder to do it locally.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 这不是电脑性能弱的问题。
cues.en: It’s not a problem of weaker computers.

cues.zh: 只是比如说，如果你在一家大公司，你有大公司的代码库。
cues.en: It’s just that for example, if you’re some big company, you have big company code base.

cues.zh: 即使在最强的MacBook Pro上，处理大公司的代码库真的很难。
cues.en: It’s just really hard to process big company code base even on the beefiest MacBook Pros.

cues.zh: 这甚至无关乎你是不是只是个学生。
cues.en: It’s not even a matter of if you’re just a student or something.

cues.zh: 我觉得即使你是大公司里最顶尖的程序员，体验依然会很糟糕。
cues.en: I think if you’re the best programmer at a big company, you’re still going to have a horrible experience.

cues.zh: 如果你能在本地做的都本地做，勉强应付，但话说回来，那就不好玩了。
cues.en: If you do everything locally where you could do it and scrape by, but again, it wouldn’t be fun anymore.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 比如近似最近邻搜索，加上这么庞大的代码库，会耗尽你的内存和CPU，而且就是基于这个。
cues.en: Like at approximate nearest neighbors and this massive code base is going to just eat up your memory and your CPU, and it’s based off of that.

cues.zh: 就是这样。
cues.en: That’s just that.

cues.zh: 我们再聊聊建模方面，正如Arvid所说，本地模型面临巨大阻力，其一，趋势似乎走向MOE，其好处之一是更受内存带宽限制，这对本地运行有利，相比使用GPU或Nvidia GPU。
cues.en: Let’s talk about also the modeling side where, as Arvid said, there are these massive headwinds against local models where one, things that seem to move towards MOEs, which one benefit is maybe their more memory bandwidth bound, which plays in favor of local versus using GPUs or using Nvidia GPUs.

cues.zh: 但缺点是，这些模型总体上就是更大了，而且它们往往需要装进不止一个节点，而是多个节点。
cues.en: But the downside is, these models are just bigger in total, and they’re going to need to fit, often not even on a single node but multiple nodes.

cues.zh: 那根本不可能装进哪怕是非常好的 MacBook 里。
cues.en: There’s no way that’s going to fit inside of even really good MacBooks.

cues.zh: 我觉得尤其是在编程方面，问题不太在于模型是否达到了某个门槛、够不够好来做这些事，然后我们就满意了？
cues.en: I think especially for coding, it’s not a question as much of, does it clear some bar of the model’s good enough to do these things and then we’re satisfied?

cues.zh: 其他问题可能是这样，也许这正是本地模型发光的地方，但人们总是会想要最好的、最聪明的、最有能力的东西，而这对几乎所有人来说，在本地运行都会非常非常难。
cues.en: Which may be the case for other problems and maybe where local models shine, but people are always going to want the best, the most intelligent, the most capable things, and that’s going to be really, really hard to run for almost all people, locally.

cues.zh: 你难道不想要最有能力的模型吗？
cues.en: Don’t you want the most capable model?

cues.zh: 你也想要[听不清 01:38:55]吗？
cues.en: You want [inaudible 01:38:55] too?

cues.zh: 还有 o1——
cues.en: And also o1-

cues.zh: 我喜欢你这样向我推销。
cues.en: I like how you’re pitching me.

cues.zh: o1 是另一个——
cues.en: o1 is another-

cues.zh: 你会满足于一个较差的模型吗？
cues.en: Would you be satisfied with an inferior model?

cues.zh: 听着，是的，我就是那种人，但有些人喜欢在本地做事，尤其是像……真的，显然有一整个开源运动在抵制。
cues.en: Listen, yes, I’m one of those, but there’s some people that like to do stuff locally, especially like… Really, there’s a whole obviously open source movement that resists.

cues.zh: 它们存在其实是好事，因为你想抵制那些正在壮大的权力中心——
cues.en: It’s good that they exist actually because you want to resist the power centers that are growing our-

cues.zh: 其实有一种本地模型的替代方案，我特别喜欢。
cues.en: There’s actually an alternative to local models that I am particularly fond of.

cues.zh: 我觉得它仍处于研究阶段，但你可以想象用同态加密来做语言模型推理。
cues.en: I think it’s still very much in the research stage, but you could imagine to do homomorphic encryption for language model inference.

cues.zh: 你在本地机器上加密输入，然后发送上去，服务器就可以利用算力。
cues.en: So you encrypt your input on your local machine, then you send that up, and then the server can use loss of computation.

cues.zh: 他们可以在这些加密数据上运行你本地跑不了的模型，但他们看不到数据内容，然后他们把答案发回来，你解密答案，只有你能看到答案。
cues.en: They can run models that you cannot run locally on this encrypted data, but they cannot see what the data is, and then they send back the answer and you decrypt the answer and only you can see the answer.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得这还处于研究阶段，重点都是想办法降低开销，因为现在开销真的很大，但如果你能做到，我觉得那会非常非常酷，也会非常有影响力，因为我觉得真正令人担忧的一点是，随着这些模型越来越好，它们在经济上会越来越有用。
cues.en: So I think that’s still very much research and all of it is about trying to make the overhead lower because right now, the overhead is really big, but if you can make that happen, I think that would be really, really cool, and I think it would be really, really impactful because I think one thing that’s actually worrisome is that, as these models get better and better, they’re going to become more and more economically useful.

cues.zh: 于是世界上越来越多的信息和数据会流经一两个中心化的参与者。
cues.en: So more and more of the world’s information and data will flow through one or two centralized actors.

cues.zh: 然后就有人担心，会有传统的黑客攻击尝试，但更可怕的是，如果世界上所有信息都以明文流经一个节点，就可能出现非常糟糕的监控。
cues.en: And then there are worries about, there can be traditional hacker attempts, but it also creates this scary part where if all of the world’s information is flowing through one node in plaintext, you can have surveillance in very bad ways.

cues.zh: 有时这会发生，因为……最初，会有充分的理由。
cues.en: Sometimes that will happen for… Initially, will be good reasons.

cues.zh: 人们会想防范恶意行为者滥用AI模型，然后你就会加入一些监控代码。
cues.en: People will want to try to protect against bad actors using AI models in bad ways, and then you will add in some surveillance code.

cues.zh: 接着其他人也会介入，你就踏上了滑坡，然后开始用大量全球数据做坏事。
cues.en: And then someone else will come in and you’re on a slippery slope, and then you start doing bad things with a lot of the world’s data.

cues.zh: 所以我非常希望我们能解决同态加密，用于——
cues.en: So I am very hopeful that we can solve homomorphic encryption for-

cues.zh: 是的，而且——
cues.en: Yeah, and-

cues.zh: ……语言模型推理。
cues.en: … language model inference.

cues.zh: ……做隐私保护的机器学习。
cues.en: … doing privacy, preserving machine learning.

cues.zh: 但我想说，这就是如今所有软件面临的挑战。
cues.en: But I would say, that’s the challenge we have with all software these days.

cues.zh: 就像云端能提供如此多的功能，我们越来越依赖它，让生活变得很棒。
cues.en: It’s like there’s so many features that can be provided from the cloud and all us increasingly rely on it and make our life awesome.

cues.zh: 但也有弊端，这就是为什么你要依靠真正强大的安全性来防范基本攻击。
cues.en: But there’s downsides, and that’s why you rely on really good security to protect from basic attacks.

cues.zh: 但控制这些数据的也只有少数几家公司，它们显然有筹码，也可能以各种方式被渗透。
cues.en: But there’s also only a small set of companies that are controlling that data, and they obviously have leverage and they could be infiltrated in all kinds of ways.

cues.zh: 这就是我们身处的世界。
cues.en: That’s the world we live in.

cues.zh: 所以这——
cues.en: So it’s-

cues.zh: 是啊，我真正担心的是这样一种世界……Anthropic有一套负责任扩展政策，我们处于较低的ASL，也就是Anthropic安全级别之类的模型分级。
cues.en: Yeah, the thing I’m just actually quite worried about is the world where… Anthropic has this responsible scaling policy where we’re the low ASLs, which is the Anthropic security level or whatever of the models.

cues.zh: 但当我们达到ASL-3、ASL-4，或任何非常强大的模型级别时……但出于大多合理的安全考虑，你会想监控所有提示词。
cues.en: But as we get to ASL-3, ASL-4, whatever models which are very powerful… But for mostly reasonable security reasons, you would want to monitor all the prompts.

cues.zh: 但我觉得这很合理、也能理解，各方的出发点都是好的。
cues.en: But I think that’s reasonable and understandable where everyone is coming from.

cues.zh: 但天哪，如果全世界的信息都被如此严密监控，那真的太可怕了，太集中化了。
cues.en: But man, it’d be really horrible if all the world’s information is monitored that heavily, it’s way too centralized.

cues.zh: 这就像走一条很细的线，一边是不想让模型失控。
cues.en: It’s like this really fine line you’re walking where on the one side, you don’t want the models to go rogue.

cues.zh: 另一边是，人类嘛……我不确定是否放心让全世界的信息都经过三家模型提供商。
cues.en: On the other side, humans like… I don’t know if I trust all the world’s information to pass through three model providers.

cues.zh: 你觉得为什么这和云服务商不一样？
cues.en: Why do you think it’s different than cloud providers?

cues.zh: 因为我觉得很多这类数据本来根本不会交给云服务商，而这里往往是……你想给AI模型更多数据，你想把那些你本来绝不会放到网上的个人数据，交给这些公司或这些模型。
cues.en: Because I think a lot of this data would never have gone to the cloud providers in the first place where this is often… You want to give more data to the AI models, you want to give personal data that you would never have put online in the first place to these companies or to these models.

cues.zh: 它还会集中控制权，而现在用云服务，你通常可以用自己的加密密钥，AWS其实做不了什么。
cues.en: It also centralizes control where right now, for cloud, you can often use your own encryption keys, and AWS can’t really do much.

cues.zh: 但在这里，只是中心化的执行者能看到所有内容的明文。
cues.en: But here, it’s just centralized actors that see the exact plain text of everything.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 说到上下文这个话题，这其实一直让我挺头疼的。
cues.en: On the topic of a context, that’s actually been a friction for me.

cues.zh: 我在用 Python 写代码时，会导入一堆东西。
cues.en: When I’m writing code in Python, there’s a bunch of stuff imported.

cues.zh: 你大概能猜到我想把哪些东西放进上下文里。
cues.en: You could probably intuit the kind of stuff I would like to include in the context.

cues.zh: 自动推断上下文有多难？
cues.en: How hard is it to auto figure out the context?

cues.zh: 挺棘手的。
cues.en: It’s tricky.

cues.zh: 我觉得未来我们在自动计算上下文方面能做得更好。
cues.en: I think we can do a lot better at computing the context automatically in the future.

cues.zh: 有一点很重要，自动包含上下文是有取舍的。
cues.en: One thing that’s important to note is, there are trade-offs with including automatic context.

cues.zh: 你给这些模型提供的上下文越多，首先，它们就越慢，请求也越贵，这意味着你能做的模型调用就更少，后台能做的花哨操作也更少。
cues.en: So the more context you include for these models, first of all, the slower they are and the more expensive those requests are, which means you can then do less model calls and do less fancy stuff in the background.

cues.zh: 而且，对很多这类模型来说，如果提示里信息太多，它们就会搞混。
cues.en: Also, for a lot of these models, they get confused if you have a lot of information in the prompt.

cues.zh: 所以你纳入的上下文，在准确性和相关性上的门槛应该相当高。
cues.en: So the bar for accuracy and for relevance of the context you include should be quite high.

cues.zh: 我们已经在产品的一些地方做了自动上下文。
cues.en: Already, we do some automatic context in some places within the product.

cues.zh: 这绝对是我们想大幅改进的地方。
cues.en: It’s definitely something we want to get a lot better at.

cues.zh: 我觉得这方面有很多很酷的想法可以尝试，既包括学习更好的检索系统，比如更好的嵌入模型、更好的重排器。
cues.en: I think that there are a lot of cool ideas to try there, both on the learning better retrieval systems, like better embedding models, better rerankers.

cues.zh: 我觉得也有一些很酷的学术想法，我们内部试过一些，但整个领域也都在广泛思考：能不能让语言模型发展到这样一个地步——你实际上可以直接让模型本身理解一个新的信息语料库？
cues.en: I think that there are also cool academic ideas, stuff we’ve tried out internally, but also the field is grappling with writ large about, can you get language models to a place where you can actually just have the model itself understand a new corpus of information?

cues.zh: 最热门的讨论版本是，你能让上下文窗口无限大吗？
cues.en: The most popular talked about version of this is can you make the context windows infinite?

cues.zh: 那么，如果你让上下文窗口无限大，你能让模型真正关注到无限的上下文吗？
cues.en: Then if you make the context windows infinite, can you make the model actually pay attention to the infinite context?

cues.zh: 然后，在你让它关注无限上下文、使其在某种程度上可行之后，你能为这个无限上下文做缓存吗？
cues.en: And then after you can make it pay attention to the infinite context to make it somewhat feasible to actually do it, can you then do caching for that infinite context?

cues.zh: 你不必一直重新计算。
cues.en: You don’t have to recompute that all the time.

cues.zh: 但还有其他很酷的想法正在被尝试，它们更类似于微调，真正在模型权重中学习这些信息。
cues.en: But there are other cool ideas that are being tried, that are a little bit more analogous to fine-tuning of actually learning this information in the weights of the model.

cues.zh: 如果你在权重层面做这件事，而不是在上下文学习层面做，你可能会获得一种质上不同的理解。
cues.en: It might be that you actually get a qualitative lead different type of understanding if you do it more at the weight level than if you do it at the in-context learning level.

cues.zh: 我觉得最终会怎样发展，目前还没有定论？
cues.en: I think the jury’s still a little bit out on how this is all going to work in the end?

cues.zh: 但在此期间，作为一家公司，我们对更好的检索系统感到非常兴奋，能挑选出代码库中与你正在做的事情最相关的部分，而且我们可以做得更好。
cues.en: But in the interim, us as a company, we are really excited about better retrieval systems and picking the parts of the code base that are most relevant to what you’re doing, and we could do that a lot better.

cues.zh: 一个有趣的验证是，把这种知识直接学习到权重中，VS Code 就是一个例子。
cues.en: One interesting proof of concept for the learning this knowledge directly in the weights is with VS Code.

cues.zh: 我们处在一个 VS Code 的分支和 VS Code 中。
cues.en: So we’re in a VS Code fork and VS Code.

cues.zh: 代码全是公开的。
cues.en: The code is all public.

cues.zh: 所以这些模型在预训练时已经见过所有代码。
cues.en: So these models in pre-training have seen all the code.

cues.zh: 它们可能也见过关于代码的问答。
cues.en: They’ve probably also seen questions and answers about it.

cues.zh: 然后经过微调和 RLHF，能够回答关于代码的一般性问题。
cues.en: And then they’ve been fine-tuned and RLHFed to be able to answer questions about code in general.

cues.zh: 所以当你问它关于 VS Code 的问题时，有时它会幻觉，但有时它确实回答得相当不错。
cues.en: So when you ask it a question about VS Code, sometimes it’ll hallucinate, but sometimes it actually does a pretty good job at answering the question.

cues.zh: 我觉得这只是……碰巧还行，但如果你能专门训练或后训练一个模型，让它真正为理解这个代码库而构建，那会怎样？
cues.en: I think this is just by… It happens to be okay, but what if you could actually specifically train or post-train a model such that it really was built to understand this code base?

cues.zh: 这是一个开放的研究问题，我们非常感兴趣。
cues.en: It’s an open research question, one that we’re quite interested in.

cues.zh: 另外还有不确定性：你是想让模型端到端地做所有事情，也就是
cues.en: And then there’s also uncertainty of, do you want the model to be the thing that end-to-end is doing everything, i.e.

cues.zh: 它在内部完成检索，然后回答问题、生成代码，还是想把检索与前沿模型分开，也许几个月后你会得到一些非常强大的模型，远超最好的开源模型？
cues.en: it’s doing the retrieval in its internals and then answering a question, creating the code, or do you want to separate the retrieval from the frontier model, where maybe you’ll get some really capable models that are much better than the best open source ones in a handful of months?

cues.zh: 然后你会想单独训练一个非常好的开源模型来充当检索器，为这些更大的模型提供上下文。
cues.en: And then you’ll want to separately train a really good open source model to be the retriever, to be the thing that feeds in the context to these larger models.

cues.zh: 你能再详细讲讲如何对模型进行后训练，让它理解代码库吗？
cues.en: Can you speak a little more to post-training a model to understand the code base?

cues.zh: 你这话是什么意思？
cues.en: What do you mean by that?

cues.zh: 这是合成数据的方向吗？
cues.en: Is this a synthetic data direction?

cues.zh: 这是——
cues.en: Is this-

cues.zh: 是的，有很多可能的方法可以尝试。
cues.en: Yeah, there are many possible ways you could try doing it.

cues.zh: 想法肯定不缺。
cues.en: There’s certainly no shortage of ideas.

cues.zh: 问题就在于进去把所有方法都试一遍，用实证的方式看哪个效果最好。
cues.en: It’s just a question of going in and trying all of them and being empirical about which one works best.

cues.zh: 一个很朴素的做法是试着复刻 VS Code 和这些前沿模型的做法。
cues.en: One very naive thing is to try to replicate what’s done with VS Code and these frontier models.

cues.zh: 那我们继续预训练。
cues.en: So let’s continue pre-training.

cues.zh: 某种持续预训练，既包含通用代码数据，也掺入你关心的某个特定仓库的数据。
cues.en: Some kind of continued pre-training that includes general code data but also throws in of the data of some particular repository that you care about.

cues.zh: 然后在后训练阶段，也就是在……先从指令微调开始吧。
cues.en: And then in post-training, meaning in… Let’s just start with instruction fine-tuning.

cues.zh: 你有一个关于代码的普通指令微调数据集。
cues.en: You have a normal instruction fine-tuning data set about code.

cues.zh: 然后你加入很多关于那个仓库中代码的问题。
cues.en: Then you throw in a lot of questions about code in that repository.

cues.zh: 所以你可以获取真实标注数据，这可能比较困难，或者你可以采用你暗示或建议的方法，使用合成数据，即
cues.en: So you could either get ground truth ones, which might be difficult or you could do what you hinted at or suggested using synthetic data, i.e.

cues.zh: 让模型针对代码的各个近期片段提出问题。
cues.en: having the model ask questions about various recent pieces of the code.

cues.zh: 所以你取出代码片段，然后提示模型或让模型为该代码片段提出一个问题，再把这些作为指令微调数据点加入。
cues.en: So you take the pieces of the code, then prompt the model or have a model propose a question for that piece of code, and then add those as instruction fine-tuning data points.

cues.zh: 理论上，这可能解锁模型回答关于该代码库问题的能力。
cues.en: And then in theory, this might unlock the model’s ability to answer questions about that code base.

cues.zh: 让我问问你关于OpenAI o1的事。
cues.en: Let me ask you about OpenAI o1.

cues.zh: 你认为这种测试时计算系统在编程中扮演什么角色？
cues.en: What do you think is the role of that kind of test time compute system in programming?

cues.zh: 我觉得测试时计算真的非常有意思。
cues.en: I think test time compute is really, really interesting.

cues.zh: 所以一直存在预训练范式，随着你扩大数据量和模型规模，它会在损失和下游基准以及整体性能上带来越来越好的表现。
cues.en: So there’s been the pre-training regime which will, as you scale up the amount of data and the size of your model, get you better and better performance both on loss and then on downstream benchmarks and just general performance.

cues.zh: 所以我们用它来做编程或其他任务。
cues.en: So we use it for coding or other tasks.

cues.zh: 我们开始遇到一些数据墙了。
cues.en: We’re starting to hit a bit of a data wall.

cues.zh: 也就是说，继续扩展这个范式会变得很难。
cues.en: Meaning, it’s going to be hard to continue scaling up this regime.

cues.zh: 所以扩大测试时计算是一种有趣的方式，如果现在增加我们使用的推理时浮点运算量，但仍然能获得……是的，随着你增加推理时使用的浮点运算量，这些模型的性能会得到相应的提升。
cues.en: So scaling up test time compute is an interesting way, if now increasing the number of inference time flops that we use but still getting… Yeah, as you increase the number of flops you use inference time getting corresponding improvements in the performance of these models.

cues.zh: 过去我们只能实打实地训练一个更大的模型，总是消耗更多的算力，但现在，我们或许可以用同样大小的模型，让它运行更久，从而得到质量堪比大得多的模型的答案。
cues.en: Traditionally, we just had to literally train a bigger model that always used that many more flops, but now, we could perhaps use the same size model and run it for longer to be able to get an answer at the quality of a much larger model.

cues.zh: 我觉得真正有意思的是，有些问题可能需要一个在100万亿token上训练的、拥有100万亿参数智能的模型。
cues.en: So the really interesting thing I like about this is there are some problems that perhaps require 100 trillion parameter model intelligence trained on 100 trillion tokens.

cues.zh: 但那可能只占所有查询的1%，甚至0.1%。
cues.en: But that’s maybe 1%, maybe 0.1% of all queries.

cues.zh: 那么，你打算投入所有这些精力、所有这些算力去训练一个成本如此之高的模型，然后却如此低频地运行它吗？
cues.en: So are you going to spend all of this effort, all of this compute training a model that costs that much and then run it so infrequently?

cues.zh: 这感觉完全是浪费，倒不如……你训练一个能处理99.9%查询的模型，然后对于那些真正极度渴望最强智能的少数人，你有办法在推理时让它运行更久。
cues.en: It feels completely wasteful when instead you get the model that can… You train the model that is capable of doing the 99.9% of queries, then you have a way of inference time running it longer for those few people that really, really want max intelligence.

cues.zh: 你怎么判断哪个问题需要什么级别的智能？
cues.en: How do you figure out which problem requires what level of intelligence?

cues.zh: 能不能动态判断什么时候用 GPT-4，什么时候用小模型，什么时候需要 o1？
cues.en: Is that possible to dynamically figure out when to use GPT-4, when to use a small model and when you need the o1?

cues.zh: 可以，这确实是个开放的研究问题。
cues.en: Yeah, that’s an open research problem, certainly.

cues.zh: 我觉得还没人真正把模型路由这个问题解决好。
cues.en: I don’t think anyone’s actually cracked this model routing problem quite well.

cues.zh: 我们在 Cursor Tab 这类功能上有初步实现，但在 4o sonnet 和 o1 之间切换的层面，就有点棘手了。
cues.en: We have initial implementations of this for something like Cursor Tab, but at the level of going between 4o sonnet to o1, it’s a bit trickier.

cues.zh: 还有个问题是，你需要多高的智能来判断某件事对 4o 级别的模型来说是不是太难了？
cues.en: There’s also a question like, what level of intelligence do you need to determine if the thing is too hard for the four level model?

cues.zh: 也许你需要 o1 级别的模型。
cues.en: Maybe you need the o1 level model.

cues.zh: 这真的不清楚。
cues.en: It’s really unclear.

cues.zh: 但你提到了这个。
cues.en: But you mentioned this.

cues.zh: 所以有预训练过程，然后有后训练，然后是测试时计算。
cues.en: So there’s a pre-training process then there’s post-training, and then there’s test time compute.

cues.zh: 这样分开公平吗？
cues.en: Is that fair to separate?

cues.zh: 最大的收益在哪里？
cues.en: Where’s the biggest gains?

cues.zh: 嗯，这很奇怪，因为测试时计算需要一整套训练策略才能让它发挥作用。
cues.en: Well, it’s weird because test time compute, there’s a whole training strategy needed to get test time compute to work.

cues.zh: 另一个很奇怪的地方是，除了那些大实验室，甚至可能只有 OpenAI，没人真正知道它是怎么运作的。
cues.en: The other really weird thing about this is outside of the big labs and maybe even just OpenAI, no one really knows how it works.

cues.zh: 有一些非常有趣的论文，展示了他们可能在做什么的线索。
cues.en: There’ve been some really interesting papers that show hints of what they might be doing.

cues.zh: 所以也许他们在用过程奖励模型做树搜索之类的事情。
cues.en: So perhaps they’re doing something with tree search using process reward models.

cues.zh: 但没错，我觉得问题在于我们并不完全清楚它具体是什么样子，所以很难评论它适合放在哪里。
cues.en: But yeah, I think the issue is we don’t quite know exactly what it looks like, so it would be hard to comment on where it fits in.

cues.zh: 我会把它归入后训练，但也许为了让模型在测试时计算中发挥作用所花费的算力……最终会远超预训练。
cues.en: I would put it in post-training, but maybe the compute spent for this kind of… forgetting test time compute to work for a model is going to dwarf pre-training eventually.

cues.zh: 所以我们甚至不知道 o1 是不是只用了思维链，也不知道他们具体怎么用这些方法？
cues.en: So we don’t even know if o1 is using just chain of thought or we don’t know how they’re using any of these?

cues.zh: 我们什么都不知道？
cues.en: We don’t know anything?

cues.zh: 推测起来挺有意思的。
cues.en: It’s fun to speculate.

cues.zh: 如果你要做一个竞品模型，你会怎么做？
cues.en: If you were to build a competing model, what would you do?

cues.zh: 嗯。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得一个做法是，你可能需要训练一个过程奖励模型，也就是……或许我们可以聊聊奖励模型，以及结果奖励模型和过程奖励模型的区别。
cues.en: So one thing to do would be, I think you probably need to train a process reward model, which is… So maybe we can get into reward models and outcome reward models versus process reward models.

cues.zh: 结果奖励模型是传统的奖励模型，人们用它来训练语言建模，它只看最终结果。
cues.en: Outcome reward models are the traditional reward models that people are trained for language modeling, and it’s just looking at the final thing.

cues.zh: 比如你在解一道数学题，那就看最终答案。
cues.en: So if you’re doing some math problem, let’s look at that final thing.

cues.zh: 你把所有步骤都做完了，然后给它打个分，评估我们认为……这个结果的奖励是多少？
cues.en: You’ve done everything and let’s assign a grade to it, how likely we think… What’s the reward for this outcome?

cues.zh: 过程奖励模型则尝试对思维链进行评分。
cues.en: Process reward models instead try to grade the chain of thought.

cues.zh: OpenAI 去年夏天有一篇初步论文，我记得，他们用人工标注者构建了数十万规模的数据集来生成思维链。
cues.en: So OpenAI had preliminary paper on this, I think, last summer where they use human labelers to get this pretty large several hundred thousand data set of creating chains of thought.

cues.zh: 最终，我觉得除了把过程奖励模型当作影响我们在一堆样本间做选择的手段之外，我还没看到人们在用法上有什么有趣的东西。
cues.en: Ultimately, it feels like I haven’t seen anything interesting in the ways that people use process reward models outside of just using it as a means of affecting how we choose between a bunch of samples.

cues.zh: 所以在这些论文里，人们的做法是从语言模型采样一堆输出，然后用过程奖励模型给所有这些生成打分，可能还结合一些其他启发式方法，再用这个来选出最佳答案。
cues.en: So what people do in all these papers is they sample a bunch of outputs from the language model, and then use the process reward models to grade all those generations alongside maybe some other heuristics and then use that to choose the best answer.

cues.zh: 人们认为可能有效、并且希望其有效的一个真正有趣的方向，是用这些过程奖励模型做树搜索。
cues.en: The really interesting thing that people think might work and people want to work is tree search with these process reward models.

cues.zh: 因为如果你真的能给思维链的每一步打分，那你就可以分叉，探索这条思维链的多条路径，然后用这些过程奖励模型来评估你所走的这个分支有多好。
cues.en: Because if you really can grade every single step of the chain of thought, then you can branch out and explore multiple paths of this chain of thought and then use these process reward models to evaluate how good is this branch that you’re taking.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 当分支的质量在某种程度上与最终结果的质量强相关时，你就有了一个好模型，知道该走哪个分支。
cues.en: When the quality of the branch is somehow strongly correlated with the quality of the outcome at the very end, so you have a good model of knowing which branch to take.

cues.zh: 所以不只是短期，而是长期？
cues.en: So not just in the short term, in the long term?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 我认为已经完成的有趣工作是弄清楚如何正确地训练过程……或者说，已经开源、人们谈论的有趣工作，是如何训练过程奖励模型，也许是以更自动化的方式。
cues.en: The interesting work that I think has been done is figuring out how to properly train the process… Or the interesting work that has been open sourced and people I think talk about is how to train the process reward models, maybe in a more automated way.

cues.zh: 我可能说错了，可能漏掉了一些论文。
cues.en: I could be wrong here, could not be mentioning some papers.

cues.zh: 我还没看到有什么特别有效的方法，能创造性地利用过程奖励模型来做树搜索和代码。
cues.en: I haven’t seen anything super that seems to work really well for using the process reward models creatively to do tree search and code.

cues.zh: 这是一个AI安全问题，也许有点偏哲学。
cues.en: This is an AI safety, maybe a bit of a philosophy question.

cues.zh: OpenAI说他们在向用户隐藏思维链，并表示这是一个艰难的决定。
cues.en: So OpenAI says that they’re hiding the chain of thought from the user, and they’ve said that that was a difficult decision to make.

cues.zh: 他们不展示思维链，而是让模型对思维链进行总结。
cues.en: Instead of showing the chain of thought, they’re asking the model to summarize the chain of thought.

cues.zh: 他们还在后台表示，会监控思维链，确保模型不会试图操纵用户，这是一个很有意思的可能性。
cues.en: They’re also in the background saying they’re going to monitor the chain of thought to make sure the model is not trying to manipulate the user, which is a fascinating possibility.

cues.zh: 不过话说回来，你怎么看隐藏思维链这件事？
cues.en: But anyway, what do you think about hiding the chain of thought?

cues.zh: OpenAI 的一个考量，纯属猜测，可能是他们想让别人难以从他们的模型中蒸馏出这些能力。
cues.en: One consideration for OpenAI, and this is completely speculative, could be that they want to make it hard for people to distill these capabilities out of their model.

cues.zh: 如果你能访问那个隐藏的思维链，复制这项技术可能反而更容易，因为那是相当重要的数据，比如看到模型为得出最终结果所采取的步骤。
cues.en: It might actually be easier if you had access to that hidden chain of thought to replicate the technology, because pretty important data, like seeing the steps that the model took to get to the final results.

cues.zh: 所以你可能也可以基于那个来训练？
cues.en: So you could probably train on that also?

cues.zh: 这方面也有一个镜像的情况，涉及一些大语言模型提供商，同样也是猜测，但这些 API 中有些过去曾提供便捷访问，可以获取它们生成的所有 token 的对数概率，以及提示 token 的对数概率。
cues.en: And there was a mirror situation with this, with some of the large language model providers, and also this is speculation, but some of these APIs used to offer easy access to log probabilities for all the tokens that they’re generating and also log probabilities over the prompt tokens.

cues.zh: 然后，这些 API 中的一些功能被取消了。
cues.en: And then some of these APIs took those away.

cues.zh: 再次强调，这完全是推测，但其中一个想法是，那些功能被取消的原因在于，如果你能获取类似这种隐藏思维链的对数概率，那就能给你更多信息，去尝试从这些 API、从这些最大的模型中蒸馏出这些能力，转移到你控制的模型上。
cues.en: Again, complete speculation, but one of the thoughts is that the reason those were taken away is if you have access to log probabilities similar to this hidden chain of thought, that can give you even more information to try and distill these capabilities out of the APIs, out of these biggest models and to models you control.

cues.zh: 有正常数据，也就是非合成数据，就是自然产生的数据，也就是说

cues.en: So having a language model, output tokens or probability distributions over tokens, and then you can train some less capable model on this.

cues.zh: 这种方法不会让你得到一个比生成这些 token 的原始模型更强的模型，但如果你想从某个非常昂贵、高延迟的模型中激发出某种能力，它非常有用。
cues.en: This approach is not going to get you a more capable model than the original one that has produced the tokens, but it’s really useful for if there’s some capability you want to elicit from some really expensive high-latency model.

cues.zh: 然后你可以把它蒸馏成一个更小的、针对特定任务的模型。
cues.en: You can then distill that down into some smaller task-specific model.

cues.zh: 第二种情况是，问题的某个方向比反方向更容易。
cues.en: The second kind is when one direction of the problem is easier than the reverse.

cues.zh: 一个很好的例子是 bug 检测，就像我们之前提到的，引入看起来合理的 bug 比真正检测出它们要容易得多。
cues.en: So a great example of this is bug detection, like we mentioned earlier, where it’s a lot easier to introduce reasonable-looking bugs than it is to actually detect them.

cues.zh: 对人类来说可能也是如此。
cues.en: And this is probably the case for humans too.

cues.zh: 所以你可以做的是，用一个没有经过大量数据训练、不那么聪明的模型，在代码中引入一堆 bug。
cues.en: And so what you can do, is you can get a model that’s not trained in that much data, that’s not that smart, to introduce a bunch of bugs and code.

cues.zh: 然后你可以用这些合成数据来训练一个非常擅长检测 bug 的模型。
cues.en: And then you can use that to then train… Use the synthetic data to train a model that can be really good at detecting bugs.

cues.zh: 我认为最后一类，也是大型实验室在合成数据方面主要在做的事情，就是用语言模型生成文本，然后可以很容易地对其进行验证。
cues.en: The last category I think is, I guess the main one that it feels like the big labs are doing for synthetic data, which is producing text with language models that can then be verified easily.

cues.zh: 一个极端的例子是，如果你有一个验证系统，能检测语言是否达到莎士比亚水平，然后你有一群猴子在打字机上打字。
cues.en: So extreme example of this is if you have a verification system that can detect if language is Shakespeare level, and then you have a bunch of monkeys typing and typewriters.

cues.zh: 你最终能获得足够的训练数据，来训练一个莎士比亚水平的语言模型。
cues.en: You can eventually get enough training data to train a Shakespeare-level language model.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，这在数学领域非常适用，因为对于形式语言来说，验证实际上非常非常容易。
cues.en: And I mean this is very much the case for math where verification is actually really, really easy for formal languages.

cues.zh: 然后你可以做的是，用一个还不错的模型生成大量推演，然后选出那些你知道确实证明了真实定理的，再进一步训练。
cues.en: And then what you can do, is you can have an okay model, generate a ton of rollouts, and then choose the ones that you know have actually proved the ground truth theorems, and train that further.

cues.zh: 对于代码，你也可以做类似的事情，比如 LeetCode 类问题，如果你有一组测试，你知道通过这些测试就意味着真正解决了问题。
cues.en: There’s similar things you can do for code with lead code like problems, where if you have some set of tests that you know correspond to if something passes these tests, it actually solved problem.

cues.zh: 你也可以这样做：先验证它通过了测试，然后用那些通过测试的输出训练模型。
cues.en: You could do the same thing where you verify that it’s passed the test and then train the model in the outputs that have passed the tests.

cues.zh: 我觉得要让这在所有领域都行得通，或者说在一般情况下行得通，会有点棘手。
cues.en: I think it’s going to be a little tricky getting this to work in all domains, or just in general.

cues.zh: 面对开放式、五花八门的任务，想要有一个完美的验证器，真的真的很难。
cues.en: Having the perfect verifier feels really, really hard to do with just open-ended miscellaneous tasks.

cues.zh: 你给模型更长期的任务，即使在编程领域也是如此。
cues.en: You give the model or more long horizon tasks, even in coding.

cues.zh: 那是因为你没 Arvid 那么乐观。
cues.en: That’s because you’re not as optimistic as Arvid.

cues.zh: 不过对，所以第三类确实需要一个验证器。
cues.en: But yeah, so yeah, that third category requires having a verifier.

cues.zh: 验证这件事，最好的情况是你确凿地知道它是对的。
cues.en: Verification, it feels like it’s best when you know for a fact that it’s correct.

cues.zh: 那样就不是用语言模型来验证了。
cues.en: And then it wouldn’t be like using a language model to verify.

cues.zh: 而是用测试或形式化系统。
cues.en: It would be using tests or formal systems.

cues.zh: 或者直接把它跑起来。
cues.en: Or running the thing too.

cues.zh: 做人工验证，就是手动做质量控制。
cues.en: Doing the human form of verification, where you just do manual quality control.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 但语言模型版本的做法是，它实际运行这个东西，并且真正理解输出。
cues.en: But the language model version of that, where it’s running the thing and it actually understands the output.

cues.zh: 对。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.en: No, that’s-

cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: I think that’s the category that is most likely to result in massive gains.

cues.zh: 那带反馈的强化学习呢，RLHF 对比 RLAIF？
cues.en: What about RL with feedback side RLHF versus RLAIF?

cues.zh: RLHF 是指你使用的奖励模型，是用从人类反馈中收集的一些标签训练出来的。
cues.en: So RLHF is when the reward model you use is trained from some labels you’ve collected from humans giving feedback.

cues.zh: 我认为，如果你能针对你关心的这类任务获得大量人类反馈，这个方法就有效。
cues.en: I think this works if you have the ability to get a ton of human feedback for this kind of task that you care about.

cues.zh: RLAIF 很有意思，因为你依赖的是……实际上，它依赖的前提是验证确实比生成容易不少。
cues.en: RLAIF is interesting because you’re depending on… This is actually, it’s depending on the constraint that verification is actually a decent bit easier than generation.

cues.zh: 因为感觉就像，好吧，你在干什么？
cues.en: Because it feels like, okay, what are you doing?

cues.zh: 你是不是在用这个语言模型去查看语言模型的输出，然后再来证明这个语言模型？
cues.en: Are you using this language model to look at the language model outputs and then prove the language model?

cues.zh: 但不对，如果语言模型验证某个解决方案比生成它要容易得多，那这实际上可能行得通。
cues.en: But no, it actually may work if the language model has a much easier time verifying some solution than it does generating it.

cues.zh: 那样的话，你或许真能得到这种递归循环。
cues.en: Then you actually could perhaps get this kind of recursive loop.

cues.zh: 但我觉得它不会完全长成那样。
cues.en: But I don’t think it’s going to look exactly like that.

cues.zh: 你还可以做的另一件事，也是我们某种程度上在做的，是把 RLAIF 和 RLHF 稍微混合一下，通常模型其实相当正确，这里的情况是先驱式挑选，在两个可能的生成结果之间选出哪个更好。
cues.en: The other thing you could do, that we kind of do, is a little bit of a mix of RLAIF and RLHF, where usually the model is actually quite correct and this is the case of precursor tap picking between two possible generations of what is the better one.

cues.zh: 然后它只需要一点点人工引导，大概 50、100 个样本的量级，就能把模型已有的先验精确对齐到你所想要的样子。
cues.en: And then it just needs a little bit of human nudging with only on the order 50, 100 examples to align that prior the model has with exactly with what you want.

cues.zh: 这和我认为正常的 RLHF 不太一样，通常你要用大量样本训练这些奖励模型。
cues.en: It looks different than I think normal RLHF where you’re usually training these reward models in tons of examples.

cues.zh: 当你比较生成与验证，或者生成与排序时，你的直觉是什么？

cues.en: Is ranking way easier than generation?

cues.zh: 它们是什么，你认为现在处于什么阶段，以及你觉得未来会怎样？
cues.en: What are they, where’d you think stand, and where do you think things are going?

cues.zh: 我觉得这很有意思。

cues.zh: OpenAI最初那篇缩放定律论文稍微有点错误。

cues.zh: 因为我觉得他们在学习率调度方面有些问题。
cues.en: Because I think of some issues they did with learning right schedules.

cues.zh: 然后Chinchilla展示了一个更正确的版本。
cues.en: And then Chinchilla showed a more correct version.

cues.zh: 后来人们又偏离了计算最优的做法。
cues.en: And then from then people have again deviated from doing the compute optimal thing.

cues.zh: 因为现在人们开始更多地针对推理预算做优化，让模型在给定推理预算下表现得足够好。
cues.en: Because people start now optimizing more so for making the thing work really well given an inference budget.

cues.zh: 我觉得这些曲线涉及的维度比我们最初用的多得多，最初我们只考虑计算量、参数数量和数据量。
cues.en: And I think there are a lot more dimensions to these curves than what we originally used, of just compute number of parameters and data.

cues.zh: 推理计算量显然是其中一个。
cues.en: Like inference compute is the obvious one.

cues.zh: 上下文长度也是一个明显的维度。
cues.en: I think context length is another obvious one.

cues.zh: 因为它们在超长上下文下要便宜得多、快得多。
cues.en: Because they’re much, much cheaper and faster at super, super long context.

cues.zh: 即便它在训练时的扩展性可能差 10 倍，也就是说你要多花 10 倍计算量才能训练出同等能力的模型，那也值得。
cues.en: And even if, maybe it was 10 X more scaling properties during training, meaning you spend 10 X more compute to train the thing to get the same level of capabilities, it’s worth it.

cues.zh: 因为大家最关心的就是超长上下文窗口下的推理预算。
cues.en: Because you care most about that inference budget for really long context windows.

cues.zh: 所以看看大家怎么玩转这些维度会很有意思。
cues.en: So it’ll be interesting to see how people play with all these dimensions.

cues.zh: 是啊，你显然谈到了多个维度。

cues.zh: 最初的想法只是看模型规模这个变量，用参数量衡量，以及数据规模这个变量，用 token 数衡量，然后看两者的比例。

cues.zh: 我认为人们可能会走的路径是……我特别看好蒸馏。

cues.zh: 如果你砸下重金训练，能调多少参数，才能得到最有能力又便宜的模型。
cues.en: And how many knobs can you turn to, if we spend a ton, ton of money on training, get the most capable cheap model.

cues.zh: 或者就是把 7B 模型往死里过训练，用远超必要最优量的 token 数量。
cues.en: Or just over-training the shit out of 7B models on way, way, way more tokens than is essential optimal.

cues.zh: 但如果你真的很在意，也许该做的是 Gamma 的做法：不光用 token 训练，而是直接用 gemma 27B 的分布来最小化 KL 散度，对吧？
cues.en: But if you really care about it, maybe the thing to do is what Gamma did, which is let’s not just train on tokens, let’s literally train on minimizing the KL divergence with the distribution of gemma 27B, right?

cues.zh: 所以知识蒸馏就在这里。
cues.en: So knowledge distillation there.

cues.zh: 你花计算资源去训练这个 270 亿参数的模型，用上所有这些 token，只是为了得到这个，我也不知道，更小的模型。
cues.en: And you’re spending the compute of literally training this 27 billion parameter model on all these tokens, just to get out this, I don’t know, smaller model.

cues.zh: 而蒸馏给你的只是一个更快的模型，更小意味着更快。
cues.en: And the distillation gives you just a faster model, smaller means faster.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 理论上，蒸馏我觉得是从你训练的数据中提取更多信号。
cues.en: Distillation in theory is, I think, getting out more signal from the data that you’re training on.

cues.zh: 这也许是另一种方式，不能完全跨越，但能部分帮助应对数据墙。
cues.en: And it’s perhaps another way of getting over, not completely over, but partially helping with the data wall.

cues.zh: 当你只有这么多数据可训练时，让我们在这个所有 token 上训练这个非常非常大的模型，然后我们再把它蒸馏成这个小一点的模型。
cues.en: Where you only have so much data to train on, let’s train this really, really big model on all these tokens and we’ll distill it into this smaller one.

cues.zh: 也许对于这个小得多的模型，我们能比最初直接训练它时，每个 token 获得更多信号。
cues.en: And maybe we can get more signal per token for this much smaller model than we would’ve originally if we trained it.

cues.zh: 我是说，你没法买座岛什么的。
cues.en: I mean you can’t buy an island or whatever.

cues.zh: 你会怎么分配，是改进大模型，还是花钱做RLHF里的人反馈？
cues.en: How would you allocate it in terms of improving the big model versus maybe paying for HF in the RLHF?

cues.zh: 或者——
cues.en: Or-

cues.zh: 对对对。
cues.en: Yeah, yeah.

cues.zh: 我觉得训练这些大模型有很多秘密和细节我根本不知道，只有大型实验室才掌握。
cues.en: I think there’s a lot of these secrets and details about training these large models that I just don’t know, and are only privy to the large labs.

cues.zh: 问题是，就算我尝试去做，也会浪费掉大量资金，因为我不了解那些东西。
cues.en: And the issue is, I would waste a lot of that money if I even attempted this, because I wouldn’t know those things.

cues.zh: 先放下诸多怀疑，假设你掌握了那些诀窍，或者你是说必须在目前有限的信息下操作——
cues.en: Suspending a lot of disbelief and assuming you had the know- how, or if you’re saying you have to operate with the limited information you have now-

cues.zh: 不不不。
cues.en: No, no, no.

cues.zh: 其实我是说，你空降进去，拿到所有信息、所有小窍门、所有小参数，所有决定训练方式的各种参数。
cues.en: Actually, I would say you swoop in and you get all the information, all the little heuristics, all the little parameters, all the parameters that define how the thing is trained.

cues.zh: 嗯哼。
cues.en: Mm-hmm.

cues.zh: 如果我们看看未来五年如何投资资金，以最大化你所说的原始智能——
cues.en: If we look in how to invest money for the next five years in terms of maximizing what you called raw intelligence-

cues.zh: 我的意思是，答案不是很简单吗？
cues.en: I mean, isn’t the answer really simple?

cues.zh: 你只要尽可能多地获取算力。
cues.en: You just try to get as much compute as possible.

cues.zh: 归根结底，你需要买的只是GPU。
cues.en: At the end of the day all you need to buy, is the GPUs.

cues.zh: 然后研究人员可以找到所有……你可以调整是想预训练一个大模型还是小模型。
cues.en: And then the researchers can find all… You can tune whether you want to pre-train a big model or a small model.

cues.zh: 这就涉及到一个问题：你真的是受限于算力和资金，还是受限于其他这些东西？
cues.en: Well this gets into the question of are you really limited by compute and money, or are you limited by these other things?

cues.zh: 我更倾向于Arvid的看法，即我们多少是受想法限制的，但总有那种——
cues.en: I’m more privy to Arvid’s belief that we’re sort of idea-limited, but there’s always that like-

cues.zh: 但如果你有大量算力，你就能做大量实验。
cues.en: But if you have a lot of compute, you can run a lot of experiments.

cues.zh: 所以你会做大量实验，还是用那些算力去训练一个巨大的模型？
cues.en: So you would run a lot of experiments versus use that compute to trend a gigantic model?

cues.zh: 我会的，但我确实相信我们在想法上是有限的。
cues.en: I would, but I do believe that we are limited in terms of ideas that we have.

cues.zh: 我觉得是的，因为即使有所有这些算力和你能在世界上收集到的所有数据，我认为你最终真正受限的甚至不是想法，而是真正优秀的工程。
cues.en: I think yeah, because even with all this compute and all the data you could collect in the world, I think you really are ultimately limited by not even ideas, but just really good engineering.

cues.zh: 即使有世界上所有的资本，你真的能组建起……世界上真正能在这里做出改变的人并没有那么多。
cues.en: Even with all the capital in the world, would you really be able to assemble… There aren’t that many people in the world who really can make the difference here.

cues.zh: 而且研究中有大量的工作，那纯粹是非常非常艰难的工程工作。
cues.en: And there’s so much work that goes into research that is just pure, really, really hard engineering work.

cues.zh: 举个非常粗略的例子，如果你看最初的 Transformer 论文，把文献中这些非常有趣的概念整合在一起做了多少工作，相比之下，然后去写所有的代码，也许是 CUDA 内核，也许是别的什么。
cues.en: As a very hand-wavy example, if you look at the original Transformer paper, how much work was joining together a lot of these really interesting concepts embedded in the literature, versus then going in and writing all the codes, maybe the CUDA kernels, maybe whatever else.

cues.zh: 我不知道它跑的是GPU还是TPU。
cues.en: I don’t know if it ran them GPUs or TPUs.

cues.zh: 最初的设计是为了真正吃满GPU性能。
cues.en: Originally such that it actually saturated the GPU performance.

cues.zh: 让GNOME Azure进来写所有这些代码。
cues.en: Getting GNOME Azure to go in and do all this code.

cues.zh: 而GNOME大概是世界上最好的工程师之一。
cues.en: And GNOME is probably one of the best engineers in the world.

cues.zh: 或者再进一步，比如下一代模型，让这些东西……比如让模型并行跑起来，并扩展到几千甚至几万台V100上，我觉得GBDE-III可能就是干这个的。
cues.en: Or maybe going a step further, like the next generation of models, having these things… Like getting model parallelism to work, and scaling it on thousands of, or maybe tens of thousands of V100s, which I think GBDE-III may have been.

cues.zh: 要让这些东西真正跑起来，需要投入的工程工作量实在太大了。
cues.en: There’s just so much engineering effort that has to go into all of these things to make it work.

cues.zh: 如果你真能把那个成本降下来，也许不是降到零，而是让它容易10倍，让一个有绝妙想法的人能立刻实现他构想的新架构版本、并且在GPU上跑到50%、40%的利用率，我觉得那会极大加速研究。
cues.en: If you really brought that cost down to maybe not zero, but just made it 10 X easier, made it super easy for someone with really fantastic ideas, to immediately get to the version of the new architecture they dreamed up, that is getting 50, 40% utilization on their GPUs, I think that would just speed up research by a ton.

cues.zh: 我是说，我觉得如果你看到了明显的改进路径，就应该先摘最容易够到的果子，对吧？
cues.en: I mean I think if you see a clear path to improvement, you should always take the low-hanging fruit first, right?

cues.zh: 我觉得 OpenAI 和其他所有实验室都做对了，先去摘那些最容易够到的果子。
cues.en: I think probably OpenAI and all the other labs that did the right thing to pick off the low-hanging fruit.

cues.zh: 所谓最容易够到的果子，就是你可以扩展到 GPT-4.25 的规模，然后一直扩，效果就一直变好。
cues.en: Where the low-hanging fruit is like, you could scale up to a GPT-4.25 scale and you just keep scaling, and things keep getting better.

cues.zh: 只要……当一切都运转良好时，去试验新想法是没意义的。
cues.en: And as long as… There’s no point of experimenting with new ideas when everything is working.

cues.zh: 你就该埋头猛干，尽可能榨出每一滴油水。
cues.en: And you should sort of bang on and to try to get as much as much juice out of the possible.

cues.zh: 然后也许当你真的需要新想法的时候……我觉得如果你要花 10 万亿美元，你大概会想花点……到那时候其实该稍微重新评估一下你的想法了。
cues.en: And then maybe when you really need new ideas for… I think if you’re spending $10 trillion, you probably want to spend some… Then actually reevaluate probably your idea a little bit at that point.

cues.zh: 我想我们都相信，要达到AGI，很可能需要新的想法。
cues.en: I think all of us believe new ideas are probably needed to get all the way there to AGI.

cues.zh: 我们大概也都相信，存在一些方法能在更小规模上测试这些想法，并且相当有把握它们会奏效。
cues.en: And all of us also probably believe there exist ways of testing out those ideas at smaller scales, and being fairly confident that they’ll play out.

cues.zh: 只是对于这些实验室来说，以它们目前的处境，很难把极其有限的研究和工程人才投入到探索所有这些其他想法上，因为还有那个核心的东西，它很可能在一段相当长的时间里持续提升性能。
cues.en: It’s just quite difficult for the labs in their current position to dedicate their very limited research and engineering talent to exploring all these other ideas, when there’s this core thing that will probably improve performance for some decent amount of time.

cues.zh: 但同时，这些大实验室也喜欢赢。
cues.en: But also, these big labs like winning.

cues.zh: 所以他们就全力以赴了。
cues.en: So they’re just going wild.

cues.zh: 好，那么一个大问题，展望未来：你现在身处编程世界的中心。
cues.en: Okay, so big question, looking out into the future: You’re now at the center of the programming world.

cues.zh: 你认为编程、编程的本质在未来几个月、未来一年、未来两年、未来五年、十年会如何变化？
cues.en: How do you think programming, the nature of programming changes in the next few months, in the next year, in the next two years and the next five years, 10 years?

cues.zh: 我觉得我们非常期待这样一个未来：程序员长期处于主导地位。
cues.en: I think we’re really excited about a future where the programmer is in the driver’s seat for a long time.

cues.zh: 你们听我们稍微谈过这一点，但它强调的是速度、程序员的自主权和掌控力。
cues.en: And you’ve heard us talk about this a little bit, but one that emphasizes speed and agency for the programmer and control.

cues.zh: 能修改任何你想修改的东西，能非常快速地对你在构建的东西进行迭代。
cues.en: The ability to modify anything you want to modify, the ability to iterate really fast on what you’re building.

cues.zh: 我觉得这和这个领域里一些人正跳向的方向有点不同，那边有一个想法迷住了大家，就是你能和你的电脑对话吗？
cues.en: And this is a little different, I think, than where some people are jumping to in the space, where I think one idea that’s captivated people, is can you talk to your computer?

cues.zh: 你能让它为你构建软件吗？
cues.en: Can you have it build software for you?

cues.zh: 就像你在 Slack 上跟一个工程部门或一个工程师说话一样。
cues.en: As if you’re talking to an engineering department or an engineer over Slack.

cues.zh: 它能不能就是那种孤立的文本框？
cues.en: And can it just be this sort of isolated text box?

cues.zh: 我们不兴奋的部分原因，是我们谈过的延迟问题，但很大一块原因是我们不兴奋，是因为那意味着要放弃大量控制权。
cues.en: And part of the reason we’re not excited about that, is some of the stuff we’ve talked about with latency, but then a big piece, a reason we’re not excited about that, is because that comes with giving up a lot of control.

cues.zh: 在文本框里交流时，想说得特别具体要难得多。
cues.en: It’s much harder to be really specific when you’re talking in the text box.

cues.zh: 如果你必须像跟工程部门沟通那样，去跟一个东西交流，那你实际上就是把一大堆真正重要的决策都交给了这个机器人。
cues.en: And if you’re necessarily just going to communicate with a thing like you would be communicating with an engineering department, you’re actually advocating tons of really important decisions to this bot.

cues.zh: 这其实从根本上触及了工程的本质。
cues.en: And this kind of gets at, fundamentally, what engineering is.

cues.zh: 我觉得有些离工程稍远的人可能会认为，规格说明已经完全写好了，然后工程师过来照着实现就行。
cues.en: I think that some people who are a little bit more removed from engineering might think of it as the spec is completely written out and then the engineers just come and they just implement.

cues.zh: 无非就是用代码把东西做出来、让东西存在。
cues.en: And it’s just about making the thing happen in code and making the thing exist.

cues.zh: 但我认为很多最好的工程、我们享受的工程，都涉及大量微小的决策——关于你到底在建什么，关于速度、成本以及系统里所有其他因素之间真正艰难的权衡。
cues.en: But I think a lot of the best engineering, the engineering we enjoy, involves tons of tiny micro decisions about what exactly you’re building, and about really hard trade-offs between speed and cost and just all the other things involved in a system.

cues.zh: 只要人类仍然是软件的真正设计者，是明确自己想要构建什么的人，而不是一切由 AI 运营的公司，我们认为你仍然会希望由人类坐在驾驶座上，来主导这些决策。
cues.en: As long as humans are actually the ones designing the software and the ones specifying what they want to be built, and it’s not just like company run by all AIs, we think you’ll really want the human in a driver’s seat dictating these decisions.

cues.zh: 所以这件事究竟会是什么样，目前还没有定论。
cues.en: And so the jury’s still out on what that looks like.

cues.zh: 我觉得关于它会是什么样，有一个挺奇特的想法：你可以控制自己查看代码库时所处的抽象层级。
cues.en: I think that one weird idea for what that could look like, is it could look like you can control the level of abstraction you view a code base at.

cues.zh: 你可以指向代码库的特定部分……比如，你也许可以通过以伪代码的形式查看代码库来消化它。
cues.en: And you can point at specific parts of a code base that… Like, maybe you digest a code base by looking at it in the form of pseudocode.

cues.zh: 而且你其实还能编辑那段伪代码，然后让改动在正式编程的层面被落实下去。
cues.en: And you can actually edit that pseudocode too, and then have changes get made down at the sort of formal programming level.

cues.zh: 你可以指向软件组件中任意一段逻辑。
cues.en: And you can gesture at any piece of logic in your software component of programming.

cues.zh: 你保留编程中的文本编辑组件，保留控制权，甚至可以深入到代码层面，也可以停留在更高的抽象层级，同时还能获得这些巨大的生产力提升。
cues.en: You keep the inflow text editing component of programming, you keep the control of, you can even go down into the code, you can go at higher levels of abstraction, while also giving you these big productivity gains.

cues.zh: 如果你能在抽象栈上上下下，那就太好了。
cues.en: It’d be nice if you can go up and down the abstraction stack.

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yeah.

cues.zh: 那里有很多细节需要弄清楚，目前还只是个模糊的想法。
cues.en: And there are a lot of details to figure out there that’s sort of like a fuzzy idea.

cues.zh: 时间会证明它是否真的可行。
cues.en: Time will tell if it actually works.

cues.zh: 但我们认为，这些让人类掌控方向的控制和速度原则非常重要。
cues.en: But these principles of control and speed in the human in the driver’s seat, we think are really important.

cues.zh: 我们认为，对于某些事情，比如 Arvid 之前提到的，对于某些编程风格，你可以用聊天机器人式的方式把它交出去。
cues.en: We think for some things like Arvid mentioned before, for some styles of programming, you can hand it off chatbot-style.

cues.zh: 如果你有一个描述得非常清楚的 bug。
cues.en: If you have a bug that’s really well specified.

cues.zh: 但这不是大多数编程工作，也不是大多数人看重的那种编程。
cues.en: But that’s not most of programming, and that’s also not most of the programming we think a lot of people value.

cues.zh: 那编程的根本技能呢？
cues.en: What about the fundamental skill of programming?

cues.zh: 现在有很多人，比如年轻人，有点害怕，因为他们热爱编程，但他们担心：“如果我走这条路，我还能有未来吗？”你觉得编程这项技能本身会发生根本性的变化吗？
cues.en: There’s a lot of people, like young people right now kind of scared, because they love programming, but they’re scared about, “Will I be able to have a future if I pursue this career path?” Do you think the very skill of programming will change fundamentally?

cues.zh: 其实我觉得现在做软件是非常非常令人兴奋的时代。
cues.en: I actually think this is a really, really exciting time to be building software.

cues.zh: 我们还记得 2013 年、2012 年那时候编程是什么样子。
cues.en: We remember what programming was like in 2013, 2012, whatever it was.

cues.zh: 那时候有太多冗余的东西、样板代码，还得去查一些特别棘手的问题。
cues.en: And there was just so much more cruft and boilerplate and looking up something really gnarly.

cues.zh: 而那些东西依然存在。
cues.en: And that stuff still exists.

cues.zh: 绝对没有归零。
cues.en: It’s definitely not at zero.

cues.zh: 但今天的编程比那时有趣多了。
cues.en: But programming today is way more fun than back then.

cues.zh: 就像我们真的越来越接近乐趣的核心。
cues.en: It’s like we’re really getting down to the delight concentration.

cues.zh: 所有真正吸引人们编程的东西，比如能够快速构建东西的速度感，以及个人的掌控力，这些都在被大幅放大。
cues.en: And all the things that really draw people to programming, for instance, this element of being able to build things really fast and speed and also individual control, all those are just being turned up a ton.

cues.zh: 所以我觉得，对于做软件的人来说，这将是一段非常非常有趣的时期。
cues.en: And so I think it’s going to be a really, really fun time for people who build software.

cues.zh: 我认为技能要求可能也会改变。
cues.en: I think that the skills will probably change too.

cues.zh: 我觉得人们的品味和创意会被放大。
cues.en: I think that people’s taste and creative ideas will be magnified.

cues.zh: 可能会少一些，稍微少一点，关于样板文本编辑的部分。
cues.en: And it will be maybe less, a little bit, about boilerplate text editing.

cues.zh: 甚至可能稍微少一点关于谨慎细致的要求，而我认为这对今天的程序员来说非常重要。
cues.en: Maybe even a little bit less about carefulness, which I think is really important today if you’re a programmer.

cues.zh: 我觉得会好玩得多。
cues.en: I think it’ll be a lot more fun.

cues.zh: 你们觉得呢？
cues.en: What do you guys think?

cues.zh: 我同意。
cues.en: I agree.

cues.zh: 我很期待能够改变……最近发生的一件事是，我们想对代码库做一次比较大的迁移。
cues.en: I’m very excited to be able to change… One thing that happened recently, was we wanted to do a relatively big migration to our code base.

cues.zh: 我们之前在 Node.js 里用 AsyncLocalStorage，众所周知它性能不太好，我们想迁移到一个 context 对象。
cues.en: We were using AsyncLocalStorage in Node.js, which is known to be not very performant, and we wanted to migrate to a context object.

cues.zh: 这是个大迁移，会影响整个代码库。
cues.en: And this is a big migration and affects the entire code base.

cues.zh: [听不清 02:22:38] 和我花了，我也说不清，五天时间来做这件事，即使有现在的 AI 工具也一样。
cues.en: [inaudible 02:22:38] and I spent, I don’t know, five days working through this, even with today’s AI tools.

cues.zh: 我真的很期待这样一个未来：我只要给几个例子，然后 AI 就能把它应用到所有地方。
cues.en: And I am really excited for a future where I can just show a couple of examples and then the AI applies that to all of the locations.

cues.zh: 然后它会高亮提示，“哦，这是个新例子，我该怎么做？”然后我再明确告诉它那里该怎么做。
cues.en: And then it highlights, “Oh, this is a new example, what should I do?” And then I show exactly what to do there.

cues.zh: 而且这十分钟就能搞定。
cues.en: And then that can be done in 10 minutes.

cues.zh: 然后你就能快得多地反复迭代。
cues.en: And then you can iterate much, much faster.

cues.zh: 这样你就不用事先想太多，站在黑板前琢磨：“我们到底该怎么做，因为成本太高了？”你可以先试一下，然后发现：“哦，这其实不完全是我想要的。”之后你还能立刻再改。
cues.en: Then you don’t have to think as much upfront and stand at the blackboard and think, “Exactly how are we going to do this, because the cost is so high?” But you can just try something first and you realize, “Oh, this is not actually exactly what I want.” And then you can change it instantly again after.

cues.zh: 所以是的，我觉得未来当程序员会非常有意思。
cues.en: And so yeah, I think being a programmer in the future is going to be a lot of fun.

cues.zh: 是啊，我很喜欢这个观点……感觉编程很多时候有两种做法。
cues.en: Yeah, I really like that point about… It feels like a lot of the time with programming, there are two ways you can go about it.

cues.zh: 一种是你在前期认真思考最佳方案，然后把有限的工程时间花在实际实现上。
cues.en: One is you think really hard, carefully upfront about the best possible way to do it and then you spend your limited time of engineering to actually implement it.

cues.zh: 但我必须强调，就是要真正进入代码，试着看看它是怎么组织的，然后快速迭代。
cues.en: But I must refer just getting in the code and taking a crack at seeing how it lays out and then iterating really quickly on that.

cues.zh: 那感觉更有趣。
cues.en: That feels more fun.

cues.zh: 似乎更大的语言模型基本上能把一种编程语言翻译成另一种。
cues.en: It seems like a larger language models is able to basically translate for one program language to another.

cues.zh: 所以我的意思是，这种恐惧在于，好吧，随着这些模型越来越好，你做的创造性决策就越来越少。
cues.en: So mean the fear has to do with, okay, as these models get better and better, then you’re doing less and less creative decisions.

cues.zh: 它会不会发展到这样一个地步：你在自然语言的设计空间里操作，而自然语言成了主要的编程语言？
cues.en: And is it going to kind of move to a place where you’re operating in the design space of natural language where natural language is the main programming language?

cues.zh: PHP。

cues.en: And I mean it also brings up the question of, I think Don Knuth has this idea that some percent of the population is geeks, and there’s a particular kind of psychology in mind required for programming.

cues.zh: 而且感觉越来越多的人能够胜任出色的编程工作，这个范围可能会扩大。
cues.en: And it feels like more and more that expands the kind of person that should be able to, can do great programming, might expand.

cues.zh: 我认为不同的人编程有不同的原因。
cues.en: I think different people do programming for different reasons.

cues.zh: 但我认为真正最好的程序员，是那些真正热爱、绝对热爱编程的人。
cues.en: But I think the true, maybe the best programmers, are the ones that really love, just absolutely love programming.

cues.zh: 比如我们团队里有些人，下班回来后真的会打开Cursor，然后整晚都在做自己的副业项目写代码。
cues.en: For example, there are folks on our team who literally when they get back from work, they go and then they boot up cursor and then they start coding on their side projects for the entire night.

cues.en: And they stay up until 3:00 a.m.

cues.zh: 就为了干这个。
cues.en: doing that.

cues.zh: 他们难过的时候会说：“我真的就只想写代码。”我觉得正是这种对编程的痴迷和热爱，才造就了真正最顶尖的程序员。
cues.en: And when they’re sad, they said, “I just really need to code.” And I think there’s that level of programmer where this obsession and love of programming, I think makes, really, the best programmers.

cues.zh: 而且我觉得这类人会真正深入钻研事物的运作细节。
cues.en: And I think these types of people will really get into the details of how things work.

cues.zh: 但你按 tab 的时候，实际上是在不断注入意图。
cues.en: But what you’re actually doing when you’re pressing tab, is that you’re injecting intent all the time while you’re doing it.

cues.zh: 有时你在拒绝它，有时你在多敲几个字符。

cues.zh: 我认为编程会发生很大变化，变成“你想做的是什么？”
cues.en: And I think programming will change a lot to just, “What is it that you want to make?”

cues.zh: 这种方式带宽更高。
cues.en: It’s sort of higher bandwidth.

cues.zh: 与计算机的交流带宽越来越高，而不是像打字那样，带宽比传达意图低得多。
cues.en: The communication to the computer just becomes higher and higher bandwidth as opposed to just typing as much lower bandwidth than communicating intent.

cues.zh: 我们构建软件和模型，在实用与可能的边界上进行发明创造。

cues.zh: 我们的工作已经改善了数十万程序员的生活。”
